question: How do stopping distances and crash severity change with higher speeds?
options: a:Increase as vehicle speed increases.,b:Decrease as vehicle speed increases.,c:Are not affected by vehicle speed.
note: Higher speeds lengthen stopping distances and increase the severity and risk of injuries in a collision; increase following distance as speed rises.

question: How should you drive just after it begins to rain?
options: a:Avoid making turns and stops at high speed.,b:Test your tires' traction while going uphill.,c:Decrease the distance you look ahead of your vehicle.
note: Wet roads reduce traction; avoid sudden high-speed turns or stops and reduce speed.

question: Extra space in front of a large truck is needed so:
options: a:Other drivers when they want to slow down.,b:The truck driver has room to stop the vehicle.,c:Other drivers can merge onto the freeway.
note: Because trucks take longer to stop, leave extra space in front so the truck driver can safely stop without causing a collision.

question: Which statement about legal and over-the-counter drugs is true?
options: a:Only illegal drugs can impair your driving.,b:Any prescription drug is safe to use if you don't feel drowsy.,c:Even over-the-counter drugs can impair your driving.
note: Prescription and over-the-counter medications (including cold, allergy, and sleep remedies) can impair driving; it's illegal to drive while impaired by any drug.

question: In fog, which lights should you use?
options: a:Use your parking lights.,b:Use your high beam headlights.,c:Use your low beam headlights.
note: Low beam headlights are appropriate in fog because high beams reflect and increase glare.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: As you enter a roundabout, you should slow down and:
options: a:Yield to any car already within the roundabout.,b:Yield to any crossing pedestrians and bicyclists.,c:Both of the above.
note: When entering a roundabout, yield to both pedestrians/bicyclists and to traffic already circulating in the roundabout.

question: How often should you check your rearview mirrors?
options: a:Often to see how traffic is moving behind you.,b:Only when you are slowing down.,c:To see if a vehicle is in your blind spot.
note: Regular mirror checks help you understand surrounding traffic and anticipate needed actions; avoid staring straight ahead for too long.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If you reach an intersection but are not in the correct lane to make your intended turn, what should you do?
options: a:Continue to the next intersection to make the turn.,b:Signal the direction you want to go and wait for a gap.,c:Stop and wait until the way is clear before turning.
note: Never turn from the wrong lane. Proceed to the next intersection and make the turn from the proper lane.

question: To improve visibility in rain or fog, drivers should use:
options: a:Low beam headlights.,b:High beam headlights.,c:Parking lights.
note: Low-beam headlights help others see your vehicle and reduce the glare that high beams cause in fog or heavy rain.

question: How should you adjust driving on gravel or dirt surfaces?
options: a:Your tires grip better than on pavement.,b:You have less traction than on pavement, so slow down.,c:Visibility is better than on pavement.
note: Loose surfaces reduce traction and increase stopping distance; slow down and drive cautiously on gravel or dirt roads.

question: During adverse weather, how should you steer and brake?
options: a:Steer off the road.,b:Drive in a low gear.,c:Steer and brake smoothly.
note: In poor weather, use smooth steering and braking inputs to maintain control and avoid skids.

question: What is the best method to avoid dangerous driving situations?
options: a:Know what is happening around your vehicle.,b:Turn off the radio.,c:Always keep your eyes focused ahead of your car.
note: Constantly observe the road ahead, to the sides, and behind you so you can react early to potential hazards.

question: How can you reduce glare from oncoming headlights?
options: a:Look briefly toward the right side of the road.,b:Stay focused on the centerline.,c:Flash your high beams at them.
note: Glance briefly toward the right edge of the road to avoid being blinded by oncoming headlights, then resume scanning ahead.

question: What do "No passing zone" signs indicate?
options: a:To maintain a steady speed.,b:That it is not safe to pass.,c:To speed up slightly.
note: A "No passing zone" sign means passing is illegal in that area because visibility or conditions make passing unsafe.

question: At an intersection with a flashing yellow light you must:
options: a:Wait for the green light before proceeding.,b:Slow down and cross the intersection carefully.,c:Stop before crossing the intersection.
note: A flashing yellow light means proceed with caution after yielding to any crossing traffic or pedestrians.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: At what speed should you travel?
options: a:At the speed of vehicles surrounding you.,b:At the posted speed limit.,c:At a speed appropriate for road and weather conditions.
note: Drive at a speed that is safe for the conditions; you must never exceed the legal limit and should slow down for hazards.

question: What is the only proven method to eliminate alcohol from your system?
options: a:Drink strong coffee.,b:Wait.,c:Take a cold shower.
note: Only time allows the body to metabolize and remove alcohol; 8,Special Situations & Road Users,nothing you eat, drink, or do will speed this up.

question: A double solid yellow centerline indicates that passing is:
options: a:Allowed from both directions.,b:Allowed only from your direction of travel.,c:Not allowed from either direction.
note: Double solid yellow lines prohibit vehicles from crossing the centerline to pass in either direction.

question: Which headlights should be used in fog, rain, or snow?
options: a:Fog lights only.,b:High beams.,c:Low beams.
note: Use low beam headlights during fog, rain, or snow; high beams will reflect back and reduce visibility.

question: How should you enter the interstate from a short ramp with no acceleration lane?
options: a:Immediately enter the far-right traffic lane and speed up.,b:Use the shoulder to get up to traffic speed.,c:Speed up and enter only after identifying a gap in traffic.
note: On a short ramp without an acceleration lane, wait for a gap and then enter when it is safe; do not use the shoulder to accelerate.

question: What does Tennessee's Implied Consent Law require of drivers?
options: a:If requested, you must submit to a test for alcohol or drugs.,b:Traffic laws apply even without signs at intersections.,c:You may refuse tests for alcohol or drugs without consequence.
note: By driving in Tennessee you consent to chemical tests for alcohol or drugs if law enforcement requests them; refusal has penalties.

question: If your vehicle begins to hydroplane on water you should:
options: a:Apply the brakes firmly to prevent your vehicle from sliding.,b:Drive at a constant speed to gain better traction.,c:Slow down gradually and not apply the brakes.
note: If hydroplaning occurs, ease off the accelerator and let the vehicle slow; do not slam on the brakes.

question: If a tire suddenly goes flat while driving, you should:
options: a:Press down on the brake pedal as hard as you can.,b:Slow down gradually and not brake.,c:Rapidly pump the brake pedal several times.
note: Hold the steering wheel firmly, ease off the accelerator, and let the vehicle slow before carefully pulling off the road; avoid hard braking.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When must you come to a complete stop?
options: a:Where there is a red traffic light.,b:At any intersection where a police officer orders you to stop.,c:Both of the above.
note: You must stop at steady or flashing red lights and obey any police officer who directs traffic, regardless of signs or signals.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What should you do first before stopping your vehicle at a traffic signal or sign?
options: a:Set the parking brake.,b:Check your mirrors for surrounding traffic.,c:Press down hard on the accelerator.
note: Before stopping, check your mirrors to be aware of traffic behind and around you. Then ease off the accelerator and apply steady braking for a smooth stop.

question: What is the purpose of work zone barriers, drums, cones, and signs?
options: a:Inconvenience drivers.,b:Make drivers angry about slow traffic.,c:Keep traffic out of hazardous work zones.
note: Work zone devices guide and protect drivers and workers by directing traffic away from hazardous areas.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Which of the following is true about changing lanes?
options: a:Look over your right shoulder for a right lane change and your left shoulder for a left lane change.,b:Vehicles with two outside mirrors do not have blind spots.,c:You only need to turn and look over your right shoulder for lane changes to the right or left.
note: Signal, check mirrors, and glance over the appropriate shoulder to inspect blind spots before changing lanes.

question: When driving through work zones you should:
options: a:Maintain your normal speed the whole way through the zone.,b:Reduce your speed and be prepared to stop suddenly.,c:Increase your speed to get through the zone as quickly as possible.
note: Slow down in work zones, obey posted limits, and be prepared to stop; workers and changed traffic patterns may be present.

question: What is the minimum jail sentence upon a second DUI conviction?
options: a:Five days in jail.,b:20 days in jail.,c:45 days in jail.
note: A second DUI conviction carries a jail sentence of at least 45 days and up to 11 months and 29 days, along with other penalties.

question: Under low-visibility conditions caused by fog you should:
options: a:Turn on your high beam headlights.,b:Increase your speed so you do not cause an accident.,c:Slow down and use your low beam headlights.
note: Use low beams in fog and reduce speed; if visibility becomes extremely poor, pull off the road safely and wait.

question: After signaling and matching speed when entering the interstate, what should you do?
options: a:Expect traffic to allow you to proceed since you have right-of-way.,b:Merge carefully into the gap.,c:Wait for the lane to clear completely before merging.
note: Identify a gap, accelerate to match traffic, signal, and merge carefully into the opening when it is safe.

question: Which of these is a dangerous habit when driving through work zones?
options: a:Failing to carefully watch for workers and moving equipment,b:Both of the above,c:Tailgating another vehicle.
note: In work zones you should reduce speed, avoid following too closely, and watch carefully for workers and equipment. Both tailgating and inattention are dangerous.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If you face a green light but traffic ahead blocks the intersection, what should you do?
options: a:Don't enter the intersection until you can get completely across.,b:Partially enter the intersection to establish your right-of-way.,c:Continue into the intersection and wait for traffic to clear.
note: Even with a green light, do not enter an intersection unless you can clear it completely; blocking the intersection is illegal.

question: If you feel fatigued while driving, you should:
options: a:Increase the volume of your radio.,b:Increase your speed to reach your destination more quickly.,c:Find a safe place to park and take a short nap.
note: Signs of fatigue are a cue to stop driving and rest; a short nap can help restore alertness before continuing.

question: A solid yellow line beside a broken yellow line means:
options: a:Vehicles next to the broken line may pass.,b:Driving in both directions may pass.,c:Next to the solid line may pass.
note: Yellow centerlines separate opposite-direction traffic; if your lane is next to the broken line you may pass when safe.

question: If there is a solid yellow line on your side of the centerline, what does that indicate?
options: a:Do not pass.,b:Reduce your speed.,c:Traffic light ahead.
note: A solid yellow line on your side of the centerline means passing is prohibited. If your lane has the solid line, you must not pass other vehicles.

question: What is meant by 'distracted driving'?
options: a:Anything that causes you to pay more attention to driving.,b:Anything that takes your attention away from driving.,c:Anything that causes evasive action while driving.
note: Distracted driving is any activity that diverts your eyes, hands, or mind from driving. It is a leading contributing factor in crashes because it causes drivers to miss critical cues.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: A flashing yellow traffic signal at an intersection instructs drivers to:
options: a:Stop and proceed only when the intersection is clear.,b:Slow down and proceed with caution.,c:Come to a complete stop as quickly as possible.
note: A flashing yellow light means slow down, be alert, and proceed with caution; a full stop is not required unless necessary.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If a police officer signals you to stop while the traffic light is green, you should:
options: a:Do what the vehicle in front of you does.,b:Obey the officer.,c:Obey the traffic signal.
note: Drivers must follow directions from law enforcement even if they conflict with traffic signals or signs.

question: If you are about to be hit from the rear, which action should you NOT take?
options: a:Applying your brakes.,b:Letting go of the steering wheel.,c:Pressing your head firmly against the head restraint.
note: Do not let go of the wheel; brace against the seat and head restraint and be prepared to apply brakes to avoid being pushed into another vehicle.

question: Like alcohol and other drugs, drowsiness will:
options: a:Help you be a better driver.,b:Make you feel better.,c:Impair your judgment.
note: Fatigue reduces reaction time, awareness, and judgment in the same way that alcohol and some drugs do.

question: If your vehicle's suspension is failing, it can cause:
options: a:Vehicle control problems.,b:Squealing brakes.,c:Slack in the steering.
note: Worn suspension affects vehicle handling and control; excessive bouncing or poor control indicates suspension issues.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When entering an interstate highway you should:
options: a:Stop, check for cars, and enter when safe.,b:Check for cars and reduce your speed to 25 mph before entering the traffic lane.,c:Check for cars, increase your speed to match the flow of traffic, and merge when the way is clear.
note: Use the acceleration lane to match freeway speeds, check traffic, and merge smoothly when safe.

question: A driver's license may be suspended or revoked for:
options: a:Fraudulently altering a driver license.,b:Frequent convictions resulting in 12 or more points on a driving record.,c:Both of the above.
note: Licenses can be suspended or revoked for serious offenses such as fraud or accumulating excessive points from violations.

question: Which statement about alcohol and intoxication is incorrect?
options: a:As weight increases, more alcohol is needed to raise BAC.,b:If two people are the same weight, the person with more body fat shows intoxication first.,c:Drinking three drinks in one hour affects you the same as drinking three drinks over three hours.
note: Drinking alcohol faster produces a higher level of intoxication; the same amount consumed quickly affects you more than if spread over time.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: At an intersection with stop signs on all corners, to whom should you yield the right-of-way?
options: a:On your left.,b:Who arrived before you.,c:Across from your vehicle.
note: Proceed through a four-way stop in the order of arrival; yield to drivers who arrived before you.

question: When you see an emergency vehicle using flashing lights, what must you do?
options: a:Maintain your speed and stay in your lane until the vehicle has passed.,b:Move into the right lane and drive slowly until the vehicle has passed.,c:Pull over to the curb or edge of the road and stop until the vehicle has passed.
note: Pull over to the right edge of the road and stop, staying parallel to the curb, until the emergency vehicle has passed.

question: When is it legal to drive around or under a lowered railroad crossing gate?
options: a:Never.,b:When you can see clearly in both directions.,c:When the warning lights are not flashing.
note: Never go around or under lowered railroad crossing gates; wait until gates are raised and you can see clearly in both directions.

question: If you hit a parked vehicle and cannot find the owner, you must:
options: a:Leave a note with your name and address on the parked vehicle.,b:Call your insurance company when you get home.,c:Wait for the owner to return.
note: If you damage parked property and cannot locate the owner, leave a note with your contact information securely attached.

question: At a railroad crossing with lowered gates and flashing lights, you should:
options: a:Drive around the crossing gates if you can't see a train.,b:Come to a complete stop well behind the gates and wait until they lift.,c:Slow down and drive around the gates.
note: Stop behind lowered gates and wait until the gates are raised and you can clearly see in both directions before crossing; going around gates is illegal.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If you drive much more slowly than the flow of traffic, you will most likely:
options: a:Improve traffic flow.,b:Interfere with traffic and receive a ticket.,c:Demonstrate defensive driving techniques.
note: Driving significantly below the normal speed of traffic can impede traffic and may result in a citation.

question: To reduce the chance of hydroplaning on wet pavement, you should:
options: a:Move to the shoulder of the road as soon as it starts to rain.,b:Slow down.,c:Put on your cruise control to maintain a constant speed.
note: Hydroplaning happens when tires ride on water. Slowing down on wet roads reduces that risk.

question: Temporary signs used in construction and maintenance areas typically have:
options: a:An orange background with black writing.,b:A red background with green writing.,c:A yellow background with blue writing.
note: Work zone signs use an orange background with black letters or symbols to alert drivers to temporary conditions and hazards.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Which action is an important step before making a turn?
options: a:Check traffic in all directions.,b:Increase your speed.,c:Always move to the left lane.
note: Before turning, check to the rear and both sides to ensure it is safe to proceed and adjust speed accordingly.

question: After a minor intersection collision with no injuries, you should:
options: a:Move your vehicle out of the traffic lane, if possible.,b:Leave your vehicle in the traffic lane until law enforcement arrives.,c:Not move your vehicle for any reason.
note: If it is safe to do so, move disabled vehicles out of travel lanes to avoid causing further hazards and allow traffic to flow.

question: If your vehicle begins to skid, you should:
options: a:Turn off the ignition.,b:Brake as hard as possible.,c:Ease up on the gas pedal.
note: If the vehicle skids, ease off the accelerator or brakes and steer gently in the direction of the skid to regain control.

question: If the road is slippery, your following distance should be:
options: a:No different than normal.,b:Closer to the car ahead than normal.,c:Farther from the car ahead than normal.
note: On slippery surfaces you need extra stopping distance, so increase the gap between you and the vehicle ahead.

question: In traffic moving 50–55 mph, you're least likely to have an accident if you:
options: a:Drive a few miles per hour faster than most other vehicles.,b:Stay within that speed range.,c:Drive a few miles per hour slower than most other vehicles.
note: Traveling at a speed consistent with the flow of traffic (within posted limits) reduces the risk of collisions caused by speed differentials.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If you enter a designated left-turn lane with oncoming traffic, what should you do before turning?
options: a:Turn your front wheels to the left to be prepared to turn.,b:Signal before you arrive at the intersection.,c:Move to the left of the center lane.
note: Signal about 100 feet before turning and keep your wheels pointed straight until it is safe to turn to avoid being pushed into oncoming traffic if struck from behind.

question: If you encounter an aggressive driver, you should:
options: a:Speed up.,b:Get out of their way.,c:Challenge them.
note: Avoid escalating the situation; move out of the aggressive driver's path and allow them to pass.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If you are driving at the posted speed and the signal turns yellow as you approach, you should:
options: a:Slow down and proceed through the intersection without caution.,b:Stop before entering the intersection, if you can do so safely.,c:Speed up to cross the intersection before the light turns red.
note: A solid yellow warns the light will change to red; stop if you can do so safely, otherwise continue through cautiously.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: After passing another vehicle, when is it safe to return to the driving lane?
options: a:You are one vehicle length ahead of the passed vehicle.,b:You can see both headlights of the passed vehicle in your rearview mirror.,c:You are 50 feet ahead of the passed vehicle.
note: Only return to your lane when you can see both headlights of the passed vehicle in your rearview mirror, ensuring a safe gap.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: You should drive on the shoulder to pass another vehicle:
options: a:Under no circumstances.,b:If the vehicle ahead of you is turning left.,c:If the shoulder is wide enough.
note: Never pass another vehicle by driving on the shoulder; it is unsafe and typically illegal.

question: Which of the following will reduce blood alcohol concentration (BAC)?
options: a:Eating foods high in fat.,b:Drinking caffeine.,c:Time.
note: Only time allows the body to metabolize and reduce alcohol levels; food, coffee, or activity do not speed elimination.

question: You should not use your horn:
options: a:Near blind pedestrians.,b:When visibility ahead is limited.,c:If you might hit another vehicle.
note: Avoid using the horn around blind pedestrians; it can startle or confuse them — yield and proceed when safe instead.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: May you drive off the paved roadway to pass another vehicle?
options: a:If the vehicle ahead is turning left.,b:If there are two or more lanes traveling in your direction.,c:Under no circumstances.
note: You may never drive off the main-traveled portion of the road onto the shoulder to pass another vehicle.

question: What does a flashing yellow traffic light at an intersection mean?
options: a:Come to a complete stop as quickly as possible.,b:Slow down and proceed with caution.,c:Stop and wait for a green light.
note: A flashing yellow light warns you to slow down and proceed through the intersection with caution; you are not required to stop.

question: Before driving you should remove snow, frost, and ice from:
options: a:Just the windshield.,b:All windows.,c:Just the windshield and passenger window.
note: Clear all windows and mirrors so you have full visibility before moving the vehicle.

question: How do you keep aware of traffic behind you?
options: a:Frequently check your rearview mirror.,b:Turn and look out your back window.,c:Keep other vehicles out of your blind spots.
note: Regularly check your rearview mirror to monitor traffic behind you and anticipate needed adjustments.

question: On a roadway with a single broken white centerline, what are you allowed to do?
options: a:You may cross the centerline to change lanes.,b:You must stay within your lane.,c:You may change lanes only from the left lane.
note: Broken white lines separate lanes moving in the same direction; you may cross them to change lanes when it is safe.

question: Which of these is true about alcohol and driving?
options: a:If you can walk in a straight line after drinking, it is safe to drive.,b:Alcohol affects judgment, which is needed to drive safely.,c:If you are under the legal blood alcohol concentration limit, your driving isn't impaired.
note: Alcohol impairs judgment, decision-making, and other skills needed for safe driving, even at low levels.

question: Which roadway surface is most likely to freeze first?
options: a:A tunnel,b:A bridge,c:An intersection
note: Bridges and overpasses are exposed to air both above and below the pavement and often freeze before the adjacent roadway.

question: Which driving skills are affected by alcohol or drugs?
options: a:Reaction time and coordination.,b:All of the above.,c:Alertness and concentration.
note: Alcohol and many drugs reduce alertness and concentration, increase reaction time, and impair coordination — all critical driving skills.

question: The term "No zones" around large trucks refers to areas where cars:
options: a:Have several car lengths between their vehicle and the truck.,b:Disappear into blind spots or are so close they limit the truck driver's ability to stop or maneuver safely.,c:Have sufficient space to travel behind the truck.
note: "No zones" are the large blind spots and areas where a truck driver cannot see you or where your presence limits their stopping and maneuvering.

question: At dawn, dusk, or during rain or snow when visibility is reduced, you should turn:
options: a:On your parking lights.,b:On your headlights.,c:Up the instrument panel lights.
note: Use your headlights whenever conditions reduce visibility; if windshield wipers are needed, use low-beam headlights.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If a traffic control signal is not working, a driver should:
options: a:Come to a full stop and yield the right-of-way before entering the intersection.,b:If the intersection is clear, the driver does not need to stop.,c:Drive quickly through the intersection to get out of the way of other vehicles.
note: When signals are inoperative treat the intersection as an all-way stop: stop completely and yield appropriately.

question: What does a solid yellow arrow for turning indicate?
options: a:You should speed up to make the turn before it changes.,b:You do not need to signal to turn from that lane.,c:Prepare to stop and yield to oncoming traffic.
note: A solid yellow arrow warns the protected turn is ending; prepare to stop and yield to oncoming traffic before turning.

question: When the centerline is a broken yellow line beside a solid yellow line, what does that mean?
options: a:Passing is permitted from the lane next to the solid yellow line.,b:Passing is not permitted from either direction.,c:Passing is permitted from the lane next to the broken yellow line.
note: Traffic beside the broken yellow line may pass when safe; traffic next to the solid yellow line may not pass.

question: If you see an emergency vehicle with flashing lights behind you while driving in a city, you should:
options: a:Drive to the right edge of the road and slow down.,b:Drive to the right edge of the road and stop.,c:Stay in your lane, slow down, and let it pass.
note: Yield to emergency vehicles using sirens and lights by pulling to the right edge of the road and stopping until they pass; if in an intersection, clear it first.

question: Interstate driving requires drivers to:
options: a:Have the ability to safely drive at increased speeds.,b:Be constantly alert.,c:Both of the above.
note: Safe interstate driving demands both the ability to handle higher speeds and constant alertness to changing traffic conditions.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Unless otherwise posted, the speed limit on primary and secondary state and federal highways is:
options: a:65 mph.,b:55 mph.,c:45 mph.
note: On Tennessee primary and secondary state and federal highways the default speed limit is 55 mph unless signs indicate otherwise.

question: Which driving skills are affected by alcohol and/or drugs?
options: a:Alertness.,b:Coordination.,c:Both of the above.
note: Substances impair multiple driving skills including alertness, coordination, reaction time, and judgment.

question: Construction zone signs are typically:
options: a:Round or octagonal with black and yellow coloring.,b:Diamond-shaped or rectangular with orange and black coloring.,c:Square or rectangular with white and red coloring.
note: Temporary work zone signs use an orange background with black letters or symbols to warn drivers of changed conditions.

question: How can any amount of alcohol in the blood affect a driver?
options: a:Knowledge.,b:Judgment and physical coordination.,c:Right-of-way privileges.
note: Even small amounts of alcohol can impair judgment and physical coordination; driving may be unsafe at any BAC level and can lead to criminal charges.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When passing another vehicle you should:
options: a:Drive at the same speed as the vehicle you are passing.,b:Pass the vehicle as slowly as possible.,c:Pass the vehicle as safely and as quickly as possible.
note: Pass another vehicle safely and promptly, and return to your lane only when you can see the passed vehicle's headlights in your rearview mirror.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When crossing a sidewalk to enter traffic from an alley or driveway, you should:
options: a:Stop only if pedestrians are on the sidewalk.,b:Stop before driving onto the sidewalk or sidewalk area.,c:Expect pedestrians to yield the right-of-way.
note: When leaving a driveway, alley, or parking lot, stop before entering the sidewalk area and yield to pedestrians and traffic.

question: How many times more likely are you to cause an accident if your BAC is 0.10% than if you are sober?
options: a:Five,b:Seven,c:Three
note: A blood alcohol concentration (BAC) of 0.10% raises crash risk about seven times compared to sober driving; higher BACs increase risk even more.

question: When driving on snowy or icy roads you should:
options: a:It is safe to use your cruise control.,b:Make speed and directional changes more gradually than you would otherwise.,c:Drive as you would under normal conditions.
note: Make gradual speed and steering adjustments on ice or snow and never use cruise control, which can lead to loss of control.

question: Which is true about large trucks compared with passenger vehicles?
options: a:They are more maneuverable than passenger vehicles.,b:They take longer to stop than passenger vehicles.,c:They all have air brakes that allow them to stop quickly.
note: Large trucks require more distance to stop than passenger vehicles at the same speed; allow extra following space.

question: If you see heavy smoke covering the road ahead, what is the safest action to take?
options: a:Turn on your high beam headlights and continue.,b:Reduce speed, move as far right as possible, and stop off the roadway.,c:Turn on your four-way flashers and continue.
note: When smoke blocks the roadway, slow immediately, drive as far right as you can, and stop off the road until it is safe to proceed. Some smoke can be hazardous to breathe.

question: Where should a driver direct their attention while driving?
options: a:Stare directly in front of their car.,b:Only focus on the middle of the road.,c:Watch beside, ahead, and to the rear of their car.
note: A safe driver constantly observes the road ahead, to the sides, and behind to anticipate and respond to hazards.

question: A diamond-shaped road sign indicates:
options: a:Warning.,b:Stop.,c:Yield.
note: Diamond-shaped signs warn drivers of special road conditions or hazards ahead; they are usually yellow or orange.

question: To avoid becoming an aggressive driver you should:
options: a:Relax and concentrate on driving.,b:Tailgate the driver in front of you.,c:Drive above the posted speed limit.
note: Stay calm, focus on safe driving, plan realistic travel times, and avoid retaliatory driving behaviors.

question: When approaching a flashing red traffic light, what should you do?
options: a:Slow down and yield the right-of-way.,b:Slow down and drive carefully through the intersection.,c:Come to a complete stop, check traffic, and go when safe.
note: A flashing red light has the same meaning as a stop sign: stop, yield to traffic and pedestrians, then proceed when safe.

question: Which statement about blind spots is true?
options: a:Blind spots are eliminated if you have one outside mirror on each side of the vehicle.,b:Large trucks have bigger blind spots than most passenger vehicles.,c:Blind spots can be checked by looking in your rearview mirrors.
note: Large trucks have larger blind spots than passenger vehicles; mirrors do not eliminate all blind spots.

question: If you must make an emergency stop on an interstate, you should:
options: a:Pull off the road, turn on your emergency flashers, and stay in your vehicle, if you can.,b:Get out of your vehicle and flag down the first vehicle that passes.,c:Sound your horn at passing cars to get their attention.
note: If possible, move fully off the travel lanes, activate hazard flashers, and remain in the vehicle until help arrives for safety.

question: On seeing orange construction signs and cones on a freeway you should:
options: a:Change lanes and maintain your current speed.,b:Slow down because the lane ends ahead.,c:Be prepared for workers and equipment ahead.
note: In work zones expect workers and equipment; reduce speed and be prepared to slow or stop.

question: When must you yield to a pedestrian using a white cane or guide dog?
options: a:Only when the guide dog is leading the person across the street.,b:Only if a crossing guard is present.,c:At all times.
note: Pedestrians using a white cane or guide dog must be given the right-of-way at all times; always yield to them.

question: When a stopped school bus ahead is loading or unloading children with lights flashing, you must:
options: a:Change lanes, drive slowly, and pass the bus cautiously.,b:Come to a complete stop until all the children have left the bus.,c:Come to a complete stop until the red lights stop flashing and the stop arm is withdrawn.
note: When a school bus displays red flashing lights and the stop arm is out, all drivers must stop until the bus resumes motion and the arm is withdrawn.

question: When should you adjust your rearview and side mirrors?
options: a:Before you start driving.,b:Before you get into the car.,c:Whenever you need to use them.
note: Adjust mirrors before moving the vehicle so you have proper visibility as you begin driving.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Drivers must obey instructions given by:
options: a:Security guards patrolling parking lots.,b:Flaggers (signal persons) at construction sites.,c:Other drivers whose vehicles are broken down on the roadway.
note: Flaggers are authorized to control traffic in work zones; drivers must obey their signals and directions.

question: What effect can strong wind gusts on highways have?
options: a:They generally affect only large vehicles.,b:They only reduce visibility.,c:They can create problems for all vehicles.
note: Strong winds can affect visibility and can physically move vehicles of any size; exercise caution during high winds.

question: What do yellow center lines on a road indicate?
options: a:Traffic lanes on one-way streets.,b:Traffic moving in opposite directions on two-way roads.,c:All carpool lanes from regular traffic lanes.
note: Yellow lines mark the center of a two-way road and separate opposing traffic; solid or broken patterns indicate passing rules.

question: When is a driver's reaction time likely to be reduced?
options: a:Drinking alcohol.,b:Sleeping.,c:Working hard.
note: Alcohol slows reflexes and impairs judgment and vision, increasing reaction times and crash risk.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When you encounter a flashing yellow light at an intersection, do this:
options: a:Yield to all traffic before crossing the intersection.,b:Slow down and cross the intersection carefully.,c:Stop, then enter the intersection when it is safe to do so.
note: A flashing yellow signal tells drivers to slow down, be alert, and proceed through the intersection with caution.

question: At a railroad crossing, what should you be especially aware of?
options: a:Watch for multiple trains.,b:Watch for vehicles that must stop at all crossings (school buses, hazardous-material trucks),c:Both of the above.
note: Approach crossings with extreme caution: look for multiple trains and other vehicles that are legally required to stop at crossings.

question: When passing a row of parked cars, you should:
options: a:Expect all other drivers and pedestrians to respect your right-of-way.,b:Be prepared for a person or vehicle to unexpectedly enter your lane.,c:Drive closely to the parked vehicles to allow more room for moving traffic.
note: Leave space from parked cars because a person or vehicle may suddenly enter your lane without warning.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What action should you take when you approach a steady yellow light and haven't entered the intersection?
options: a:Speed up to beat the red light.,b:Reduce your speed and proceed carefully through the intersection.,c:Come to a safe stop.
note: A steady yellow light warns that the signal will turn red; stop safely if you have not already entered the intersection.

question: To reduce the risk of hydroplaning in heavy rain, you should:
options: a:Put your cruise control on to maintain a constant speed.,b:Decrease your speed.,c:Move to the shoulder of the road as soon as it starts to rain.
note: Lower your speed in rainy conditions so your tires maintain contact with the road and reduce the chance of hydroplaning.

question: If oncoming headlights are blinding you at night, what should you do?
options: a:Look toward the right edge of the road.,b:Switch your lights to high beams.,c:Turn your lights on and off.
note: Glance toward the right edge of the road and use lane markings as a guide to avoid being blinded by oncoming headlights.

question: When you are taking any medication, what precaution should you take regarding driving?
options: a:Keep your window open and drive more slowly.,b:Consult your doctor about the effects before driving.,c:Have someone follow you home.
note: Prescription and over-the-counter medications can impair driving. Ask your doctor or pharmacist whether a medicine will affect your ability to drive safely.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: A steady red arrow pointing right means you may:
options: a:Turn in that direction after slowing and checking for traffic.,b:Not turn in that direction until the light turns green.,c:Turn in that direction after you come to a complete stop.
note: A red arrow prohibits turning in that direction until a green signal or green arrow is displayed.

question: At what BAC can a driver under 21 have their license suspended in Tennessee?
options: a:0.15 percent or more.,b:0.08 percent or more.,c:Any detectable amount.
note: Tennessee enforces a zero-tolerance policy for drivers under 21; any detectable alcohol can lead to license suspension.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If you face a green light and there are pedestrians in the intersection, you must:
options: a:Yield the right-of-way to pedestrians.,b:Proceed because you have the right-of-way.,c:Require pedestrians to wait for you to cross.
note: Yield to pedestrians and any vehicles already in the intersection; drivers must yield to pedestrians when turning on a steady green.

question: When should you add extra following distance to the vehicle in front?
options: a:Are following a small passenger vehicle.,b:Are being tailgated by another driver.,c:Are driving more slowly than the posted speed limit.
note: If someone is tailgating you, create extra space ahead of your vehicle to allow you to slow gradually without sudden braking.

question: Driving at night is more dangerous mainly because:
options: a:You cannot see as far ahead at night.,b:The road is always more slippery at night.,c:Your reaction time is slower at night.
note: Night driving reduces how far ahead you can see, and glare from oncoming lights further reduces visibility; use headlights and drive cautiously.

question: A flashing yellow signal at an intersection means you should:
options: a:Slow down and proceed with caution.,b:Wait for a green light before proceeding.,c:Stop before crossing the intersection.
note: A flashing yellow light warns drivers to slow down, watch for cross traffic, and proceed carefully.

question: If you see a pedestrian using a guide dog or carrying a white cane you must:
options: a:Honk your horn to let them know you are there.,b:The pedestrian must yield the right-of-way.,c:You must yield the right-of-way.
note: Blind or partially sighted pedestrians using a cane or guide dog must be given the right-of-way; stop and allow them to cross safely.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What must you confirm before merging back after passing?
options: a:Beep your horn.,b:See both headlights of the passed vehicle in your rearview mirror.,c:Flash your headlights.
note: Only return to your lane when you can see both headlights of the passed vehicle in your mirror, ensuring a safe gap.

question: If poor weather reduces your visibility you should:
options: a:Speed up to get off the road quickly.,b:Drive in the lane closest to oncoming traffic.,c:Increase your following distance.
note: Increase your following distance and reduce speed when visibility is reduced to allow more reaction time.

question: Which behavior may indicate an aggressive driver?
options: a:Erratic and improper lane changes.,b:The number of passengers in the car.,c:The driver tends to drive slowly.
note: Aggressive drivers often make unsafe, erratic lane changes; avoid engaging and get out of their way.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Before changing lanes you should:
options: a:Slow down.,b:Check the inside rearview mirror.,c:Check your side mirror and look over your shoulder to make sure the lane is clear.
note: Check mirrors, signal, and glance over your shoulder to verify the blind spot is clear before moving lanes.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If you face a green light but the intersection is blocked by traffic, you should:
options: a:Turn left and find another route.,b:Stay out of the intersection until traffic clears.,c:Follow the other vehicles and enter the intersection.
note: Do not enter an intersection you cannot clear; wait until traffic ahead moves so you won't block cross traffic when the light changes.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When an emergency vehicle is using its siren and flashing lights you must:
options: a:Move into the right lane and drive slowly until it has passed.,b:Drive as closely to the right edge of the road as possible and stop.,c:Stop immediately, even if you are within an intersection.
note: Safely pull to the right edge and stop; do not stop in the middle of an intersection. Resume driving after the emergency vehicle passes.

question: What should you do when an oncoming car's headlights are blinding you at night?
options: a:Stop until the other driver passes.,b:Look below their headlights.,c:Glance toward the right edge of your lane.
note: Avoid looking directly at oncoming headlights; glance to the right edge of your lane until the vehicle passes.

question: You must stop before crossing railroad tracks when:
options: a:The railroad crossing is located in a city or town that has frequent train traffic.,b:You are transporting two or more young children in a passenger vehicle.,c:There isn't room on the other side for you to completely cross the tracks.
note: Never stop on the tracks; if you cannot clear the far side, wait until you can cross completely to avoid being trapped on the rails.

question: If you are getting tired while driving, you should:
options: a:Open a window.,b:Stop and either get rest or change drivers.,c:Drink something with caffeine.
note: If you become drowsy, stop at a safe place to rest or switch drivers; short fixes like caffeine are not substitutes for rest.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: A driver should use the proper turn signal how far before beginning a turn?
options: a:50 feet,b:75 feet,c:25 feet
note: Activate your turn signal at least 50 feet before the turn to inform other road users of your intentions.

question: What is the purpose of broken yellow centerlines on streets and highways?
options: a:Indicate no passing zones.,b:Separate lanes of traffic moving in the same direction.,c:Separate lanes of traffic moving in opposite directions.
note: Broken yellow lines separate traffic moving in opposite directions and indicate passing is permitted where the line next to you is broken.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: At intersections, crosswalks, and railroad crossings you should always:
options: a:Slowly pass vehicles that seem to be stopped for no reason.,b:Stop, listen, and proceed cautiously.,c:Look to the sides of your vehicle to see what is coming.
note: Whenever people may enter your path or traffic lines meet, scan left and right to ensure nothing is approaching from the sides.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If a pedestrian is in the crosswalk when your light turns green, what must you do?
options: a:Proceed if you have the right-of-way.,b:Proceed if the pedestrian is not in your lane.,c:Wait until the pedestrian finishes crossing before proceeding.
note: You must yield to any pedestrian in the intersection; wait until they have crossed before you proceed even if your light turns green.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Where should you position your vehicle when preparing to turn left from a two-way street?
options: a:Near the right-hand side of the road.,b:Near the centerline.,c:On the left of the centerline.
note: When turning left from a two-way street, position your car near the centerline and make 8,Special Situations & Road Users,the turn into the first available legal lane.

question: How many alcoholic drinks can affect your driving ability?
options: a:Three,b:Two,c:One
note: Even one drink can impair driving ability; it is safest not to drive after consuming any alcohol.

question: If your vehicle begins to skid, what is the recommended action?
options: a:Stay off the brakes.,b:Brake lightly.,c:Brake abruptly.
note: If your vehicle starts to skid, avoid using the brakes; braking can worsen the skid. Steer in the direction you want the vehicle to go and regain control before slowing.

question: What must drivers do at a crosswalk?
options: a:You must yield to pedestrians.,b:Pedestrians must yield to you.,c:Construction workers must yield to you.
note: Pedestrians have the right-of-way at crosswalks; vehicles must stop for pedestrians whether the crosswalk is marked or unmarked unless signals indicate otherwise.

question: If you are angry after an argument, you should:
options: a:Loudly play the radio while driving so you won’t think about your argument.,b:Drive on the interstate to let off steam.,c:Take a few minutes to cool off before driving.
note: Emotional upset can impair judgment; give yourself time to calm down before operating a vehicle.

question: Why is driving at night more hazardous?
options: a:Distance and vehicle speed are difficult to judge in the dark.,b:The speed limit is increased at night.,c:There are fewer cars on the roads at night.
note: Reduced visibility at night makes it harder to judge distances and speeds. You can only see as far as your headlights illuminate.

question: What should you do as you near the crest of a hill?
options: a:Speed up slightly.,b:Prepare to stop if necessary.,c:Maintain a steady speed.
note: You cannot see what is over the top of a hill; slow and be prepared to stop if there is a hazard.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If you and the driver on your left reach a four-way stop at the same time, who goes first?
options: a:The driver on your left has the right-of-way.,b:You have the right-of-way.,c:Whoever is signaling to make a turn has the right-of-way.
note: When two vehicles arrive at the same time, the vehicle on the right has the right-of-way — so if the other driver is to your left, you go first.

question: Driving significantly slower than surrounding traffic is:
options: a:Often a hazard because other drivers may become frustrated and try to pass you.,b:A good idea if the weather is bad.,c:Appropriate if you don’t know the speed limit.
note: Driving much slower than the flow of traffic can create unsafe passing attempts and increase crash risk; drive with the flow when safe and legal.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: At an intersection with a flashing red light you must:
options: a:Come to a complete stop, yield to oncoming traffic and pedestrians, then proceed.,b:Reduce your speed and proceed with caution.,c:Come to a complete stop and remain stopped as long as the light is red.
note: A flashing red signal functions like a stop sign: stop fully, yield as required, and proceed only when safe.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Excessive speed most often:
options: a:Does not increase the chance of a crash.,b:Increases your ability to react to a hazard.,c:Often leads to high-risk decision-making.
note: Excessive speed contributes to crashes and poor decision-making; it rarely saves meaningful time.

question: When should you begin slowing for an interstate exit?
options: a:About halfway through the deceleration lane.,b:As you approach the deceleration lane.,c:Immediately upon entering the deceleration lane.
note: Keep your highway speed until you enter the deceleration lane, then reduce speed to the advisory exit speed posted for the ramp.

question: Increase your following distance behind a large vehicle primarily to:
options: a:Because other drivers tend to pull behind large vehicles before trying to pass them.,b:To better see around the sides of the vehicle.,c:Because following too closely will get you caught in the vehicle's slipstream.
note: Extra space behind large vehicles helps you see the road ahead and gives more time to react to hazards.

question: If you are about to be hit from the rear, which should you not do?
options: a:Release your seat belt.,b:Brace yourself.,c:Press your head against the head restraint.
note: Do not release your seat belt; brace against the seat and use the head restraint to reduce whiplash and maintain control.

question: When driving in a construction zone, you should:
options: a:Slightly increase your speed.,b:Expect the unexpected.,c:Expect construction workers to yield to motorists.
note: Construction zones present changing conditions; drive with extra caution and be prepared for sudden changes.

question: What is the purpose of rumble strips?
options: a:They alert drivers to potential tire problems.,b:They test a vehicle's shock absorbers.,c:They alert inattentive drivers that their vehicles have left the travel lane through vibration and sound.
note: Rumble strips create noise and vibration to warn drivers that they are drifting out of the travel lane or approaching a hazard.

question: What does a steady yellow left-turn arrow tell drivers?
options: a:Drivers should prepare to yield to oncoming traffic.,b:The protected left-turn period is about to end.,c:Both of the above.
note: A yellow left-turn arrow warns that the protected left-turn phase is ending and you must prepare to yield to oncoming traffic.

question: On rainy, snowy, or foggy days, use your headlights because:
options: a:To warn others of bad weather conditions.,b:So others can see your vehicle.,c:To keep your engine warm.
note: Headlights make your vehicle more visible to other drivers in poor weather; if windshield wipers are needed, low beams must be used.

question: How can you help keep the driver behind you a safe distance away?
options: a:Drive 10 mph faster than the car behind you.,b:Maintain a steady speed.,c:Drive 10 mph slower than the car behind you.
note: Maintaining a steady speed and signaling well in advance helps the driver behind keep an appropriate following distance.

question: Why is it dangerous to follow a motorcycle too closely?
options: a:They do not follow the same rules as motor vehicles.,b:A motorcycle can stop much faster than a standard vehicle.,c:They brake more slowly than motor vehicles.
note: Motorcycles can stop more quickly than most vehicles; following too closely reduces your ability to avoid rear-end collisions.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: How soon before turning must you activate your turn signal?
options: a:At least 50 feet.,b:As soon as you decide to turn.,c:At least 100 feet.
note: You must signal at least 50 feet before the location of your turn to warn other road users of your intention.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: You should signal continuously when turning because:
options: a:Is illegal to turn off your signal before completing a turn.,b:It lets other drivers know what your intentions are.,c:Is always unsafe to turn off a signal before completing a turn.
note: Continuous signaling communicates your intentions to other road users and helps prevent misunderstandings and crashes.

question: Tennessee law requires children under which age to be secured in an approved child restraint?
options: a:Two,b:Four,c:Three
note: Children under age four must be in an approved child restraint; different age/weight/height rules apply for rear/forward-facing and booster seats.

question: Which best describes defensive driving?
options: a:They expect no breaks and give none.,b:They know other drivers will do the right thing.,c:They consider what other drivers might do and are prepared to react.
note: Defensive drivers anticipate possible mistakes by others and are prepared to react to avoid crashes.

question: When must you use low beam headlights?
options: a:In fog.,b:On a lighted street.,c:On a freeway.
note: Use low beams in fog, rain, snow, or mist because high beams can reflect and reduce visibility.

question: If you become drowsy while driving, you should:
options: a:Try to fight it.,b:Take some caffeine pills.,c:Take a break.
note: If you feel tired while driving, stop at a safe location to rest or switch drivers; caffeine is not a substitute for sleep.

question: When double solid yellow lines separate traffic lanes:
options: a:Passing is permitted from the right.,b:Passing is permitted from the left.,c:Passing is not permitted from either direction.
note: Double solid yellow lines indicate passing is prohibited in both directions because lanes carry opposite-traveling traffic.

question: What is the law regarding open alcoholic containers in a vehicle on a highway?
options: a:Illegal to drink from or possess open containers.,b:Legal to drink if you are not the driver.,c:Legal to drink if you are driving but not intoxicated.
note: It is illegal for drivers and passengers to possess or consume open alcoholic beverages in a motor vehicle while on a highway.

question: Which substances can impair your ability to drive?
options: a:Tranquilizers, marijuana, and sedatives.,b:Cough syrups and cold tablets containing codeine or antihistamines.,c:All of the above.
note: Many prescription, over-the-counter, and illegal drugs can impair driving; read labels and avoid driving if impaired.

question: If you experience a tire blowout, what should you do?
options: a:Tap or pump the brakes.,b:Slow down gradually and use your brakes lightly.,c:Apply the brakes firmly and quickly.
note: Ease off the accelerator and slow down gradually; do not apply heavy braking until the vehicle has slowed.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: A driver should generally:
options: a:Assume most drivers obey the right-of-way rules.,b:Assume all drivers automatically obey the right-of-way rules.,c:Always be prepared to yield the right-of-way.
note: Even when you have legal right-of-way, be prepared to yield if doing so will prevent a collision.

question: What penalties apply to driving under the influence of drugs compared with alcohol?
options: a:A lesser penalty than driving under the influence of alcohol.,b:The same penalty as driving under the influence of alcohol.,c:Absolutely no penalty at all.
note: Penalties for impaired driving are the same whether impairment is caused by alcohol or by any drug, including legal medications.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When preparing to turn left at a corner, to whom must you yield the right-of-way?
options: a:Oncoming vehicles also turning left.,b:All approaching vehicles.,c:Pedestrians on the sidewalk waiting for a "Walk" signal.
note: When turning left you must yield to pedestrians, bicyclists, and oncoming vehicles that have the right-of-way or are already in the intersection.

question: If cars are approaching on your left and parked cars are on your right, how should you steer?
options: a:Closer to the oncoming vehicles than the parked vehicles.,b:Closer to the parked vehicles than the oncoming vehicles.,c:A middle course between the oncoming and parked vehicles.
note: Take a middle course between oncoming traffic and parked vehicles to give yourself a buffer from both hazards.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: To safely enter a gap in highway traffic you should:
options: a:Speed up and let the other vehicles make way.,b:Watch only the vehicles behind the gap.,c:Check behind you, then watch the vehicle ahead.
note: Check traffic behind and to the side, then judge the gap ahead before merging into highway traffic.

question: If you are already in an intersection when the light changes from green to steady yellow you should:
options: a:Increase your speed so as not to cause an accident.,b:Stop.,c:Continue moving and clear the intersection safely.
note: If you are already in the intersection when the light turns yellow, proceed to clear it safely and promptly.

question: You approach a stopped school bus with flashing lights and the stop arm extended. What must you do?
options: a:Proceed at normal speed, but watch for children.,b:Stop.,c:Proceed at 15 mph if no children are present.
note: When a school bus has flashing lights and the stop arm extended, you must stop and remain stopped until the arm is withdrawn and the bus moves, regardless of your direction of travel.

question: If you are the operator involved in a reportable crash, within how many days must you file a report with the Department of Safety and Homeland Security?
options: a:48 hours.,b:20 days.,c:10 days.
note: An operator or owner involved in a reportable crash in Tennessee must file the required report with the Department within 20 days of the incident.

question: What is a likely effect at a BAC of 0.02%?
options: a:Won't have any effect on your driving.,b:Won't put other drivers at risk.,c:Will double your chances of having an accident.
note: Even small increases in BAC significantly raise the risk of a fatal crash; 0.02% nearly doubles that risk.

question: What does a double solid yellow centerline mean about passing?
options: a:Allowed from both directions.,b:Allowed only from your direction of travel.,c:Not allowed from either direction.
note: Double solid yellow lines indicate that passing is prohibited for traffic in both directions.

question: If you must park in a nonstandard parking area, you should:
options: a:Park with your reverse lights on.,b:Make sure your vehicle is visible to drivers approaching from any direction.,c:Park five feet from the curb.
note: When parking where vehicles don't normally stop, ensure your car is visible so it does not become a hazard to approaching traffic.

question: To reduce the chance of losing traction on wet roads you should:
options: a:Slow down.,b:Apply the brakes firmly.,c:Make abrupt turns.
note: On wet roads, reduce speed and avoid abrupt steering or braking to help maintain traction.

question: On a dimly lit street at night, how should you drive?
options: a:Drive slowly enough that you can stop within the area illuminated by your headlights.,b:Turn on your high beam headlights to better see vehicles ahead.,c:Keep instrument panel lights bright to be more visible to other drivers.
note: Drive at a speed that allows you to stop within the distance lit by your headlights to account for limited visibility.

question: How should you check your blind spot when changing lanes?
options: a:Using the side mirror.,b:Turning your head and looking over your shoulder.,c:Using the inside rearview mirror.
note: Mirrors may not show everything; turn your head and glance over your shoulder to check blind spots before changing lanes.

question: What does a curb painted red mean?
options: a:Loading zone.,b:The area is reserved for picking up or dropping off passengers.,c:No parking, standing, or stopping.
note: A red-painted curb means stopping, standing, or parking is prohibited in that area.

question: When parking downhill on a two-way road with no curb, point your front wheels:
options: a:Straight ahead,b:Right, toward the side of the road,c:Left, toward the center of the road
note: When parking downhill without a curb, turn the wheels toward the side (right) so the vehicle will roll away from traffic if the brakes fail.

question: Double solid yellow center lines mean:
options: a:Both lanes may pass.,b:Neither lane may pass.,c:The lane to the right may pass.
note: Double solid yellow lines separate opposing traffic and prohibit passing from either direction.

question: If the roadway ahead is flooded, you should:
options: a:Slam on the brakes.,b:Not drive through the flooded area; turn around and find another route.,c:Drive only in the center of the roadway.
note: Never attempt to drive through flooded roadways; even shallow-looking water can hide hazards or cause loss of control.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When merging onto an interstate highway, what should you do?
options: a:Select a safe gap and merge into the lane of traffic.,b:Always stop before entering the highway.,c:Merge across two lanes at once.
note: Match the speed of traffic and find a safe gap to merge smoothly into the flow; do not stop on the ramp unless necessary.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If you are being passed on both sides while driving in the center lane of an expressway, you should:
options: a:Stay in the center lane.,b:Move to the lane on your right.,c:Move to the lane on your left.
note: On multi-lane roads, slower drivers should move to the right lanes to allow faster traffic to pass on the left.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: A flashing red traffic light at an intersection means:
options: a:The light is about to turn green.,b:The same thing as a stop sign.,c:The same thing as a yield sign.
note: A flashing red signal requires a full stop, then yield to traffic and pedestrians before proceeding, just like a stop sign.

question: Fatigue while driving increases the risk of:
options: a:Being late for an appointment.,b:Missing an exit.,c:Falling asleep behind the wheel and crashing.
note: Driver fatigue slows reactions and can lead to falling asleep at the wheel, greatly increasing crash risk.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If the traffic signal turns red while you are in the intersection waiting to turn left, what should you do?
options: a:Stop until the light changes to green.,b:Back out of the intersection, if possible.,c:Complete the turn when traffic clears.
note: If you are already in the intersection when the signal changes, complete your left turn safely when there is no oncoming traffic or pedestrians.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Approaching an intersection showing a flashing yellow light, you must:
options: a:Maintain your normal speed.,b:Slow down and proceed with caution.,c:Come to a complete stop at the intersection.
note: A flashing yellow signal warns drivers to be alert and to slow down; proceed carefully through the intersection.

question: While driving on the highway, consistently looking far ahead helps you:
options: a:Reduce the need for last-minute braking or turning.,b:Allow you to spot upcoming police officers.,c:Help you keep up with traffic.
note: Scanning far ahead lets you anticipate hazards and make smoother, safer lane changes and speed adjustments.

question: In Tennessee, a DUI conviction is based on which blood alcohol concentration (BAC)?
options: a:0.05 percent.,b:0.08 percent.,c:50 percent.
note: Driving with a BAC of 0.08% or higher is illegal for adults; drivers under 21 face penalties at much lower BAC levels.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When merging onto the freeway, at what speed should you be driving?
options: a:At or near the speed of the freeway traffic.,b:At the legal speed limit.,c:More slowly than the freeway traffic.
note: Enter the freeway at or near the speed of traffic so you can merge smoothly; match speed unless traffic exceeds the legal limit.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Into which lane should you turn when making a left from a two-way onto a one-way street?
options: a:Turn into any lane.,b:Turn into the first lane.,c:Turn into the second lane.
note: Turn from the lane closest to the centerline into the first available lane on the one-way street unless signs indicate otherwise.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If traffic is merging into your freeway lane, you should:
options: a:Make room for the merging traffic, if possible.,b:Always maintain your position.,c:Assert your right-of-way by driving faster.
note: When safe, adjust speed or change lanes to create space for vehicles merging into your lane.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If traffic is faster behind you in the left lane, what should you do?
options: a:Stay in your lane so you don't impede traffic.,b:Drive onto the left shoulder to let the other vehicles pass.,c:Move into the right lane when it is safe.
note: If traffic behind you is faster and you 8,Special Situations & Road Users,can safely do so, move into the right lane to allow others to pass.

question: Which statement about pedal use is correct?
options: a:Use your left foot to brake.,b:You should always brake abruptly to ensure stopping.,c:Use your right foot for both braking and accelerating your vehicle.
note: Use your right foot for both the accelerator and brake to avoid accidental pedal misuse and ensure smooth control.

question: When a school bus has its red lights flashing and stop arm extended, drivers stopped behind must remain stopped until:
options: a:All students are off the bus.,b:The stop arm is retracted and the bus resumes motion.,c:The stop arm is retracted.
note: Do not pass a stopped school bus until its red lights are off, the stop arm is withdrawn, and it begins moving again.

question: In a vehicle with airbags the safest place for children age 12 and under to ride is:
options: a:The back seat.,b:The front seat.,c:The bed of a pick-up truck.
note: Children 12 and under should ride in the back seat where airbags pose less risk to small occupants.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What is the correct action if another vehicle passes you in a no-passing zone?
options: a:Pull off the road.,b:Maintain your speed and position.,c:Slow down to let the passing vehicle return to the drive lane.
note: If another driver passes you, slow down and permit them to re-enter your lane safely to reduce hazards.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When passing another vehicle it is safe to return to your lane when you:
options: a:Have passed the other vehicle’s front bumper.,b:See the vehicle's headlights in your rearview mirror.,c:Cannot see the vehicle directly to your right.
note: Return to your lane only when you can see the passed vehicle's headlights in your rearview mirror, ensuring enough space.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When parking uphill on a two-way road with no curb, which way should you turn the front wheels?
options: a:Left, toward the center of the road.,b:Straight ahead.,c:Right, toward the side of the road.
note: On a road without a curb, turn the front wheels so the vehicle will roll away from the center of the road if the brakes fail — that is, toward the roadside.

question: Having a driver's license is a:
options: a:Privilege.,b:Requirement.,c:Right.
note: Driving is a privilege granted by the state and can be suspended or revoked for violations.

question: If pedestrians are illegally crossing the street (jaywalking), you:
options: a:Should honk your horn at them.,b:Do not have to stop for them.,c:Must stop for them.
note: You must yield to pedestrians at all times, even if they are crossing outside a crosswalk; stop to avoid a collision.

question: What color are regulatory traffic signs typically?
options: a:Green.,b:Yellow.,c:White.
note: Regulatory signs indicate laws and must be obeyed; they are commonly white rectangles or squares with black, red, or green letters or symbols.

question: The two-second rule is intended to be used when driving at:
options: a:Speeds up to 55 mph.,b:Any speed.,c:Speeds up to 30 mph.
note: The two-second following rule applies generally; increase the gap to four seconds or more in poor weather or low visibility.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: To turn left from a multilane one-way street onto another one-way street, you should start your turn from:
options: a:The lane in the center of the road.,b:The lane closest to the left curb.,c:Any lane (as long as it is safe).
note: On one-way streets, begin left turns from the far-left lane so you can turn safely into the leftmost lane of the street you enter.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When merging onto the freeway you should be driving:
options: a:Five to 10 mph slower than the speed of traffic on the freeway.,b:At or near the speed of traffic on the freeway.,c:The posted speed limit for freeway traffic.
note: Use the acceleration lane to match the speed of traffic on the freeway and merge smoothly when safe.

question: When encountering slippery surfaces such as ice or snow you should:
options: a:Maintain traction by following other vehicles closely.,b:Pump your brakes to keep them from freezing.,c:Shift to a low gear before going down steep hills.
note: To reduce the risk of skids, use a lower gear when descending steep hills and increase following distances.

question: When is highway pavement most slippery during rain?
options: a:If it has been raining for one to two hours.,b:If it has just begun to rain.,c:If it has been raining several hours.
note: Road surfaces are especially slippery when rain first begins because oil and dirt on the pavement mix with water to form a greasy film.

question: Where are a truck's blind spots typically located?
options: a:On the immediate left of the cab.,b:Both on the immediate left of the cab and directly behind the body.,c:Directly behind the body.
note: Large trucks have extensive blind spots on the left side of the cab and immediately behind the truck where the driver cannot see other vehicles.

question: Because motorcycles, scooters, and mopeds are hard to see, you should:
options: a:Share a lane with a motorcycle.,b:Make constant visual checks.,c:Slow down when driving.
note: Motorcycles are often in blind spots and can be missed; drivers should scan frequently and check mirrors and blind spots.

question: As vehicle speed increases, how are stopping distance and crash severity affected?
options: a:Are not affected by a vehicle's speed.,b:Decrease as a vehicle's speed increases.,c:Increase as a vehicle's speed increases.
note: Higher speeds increase stopping distances and the potential impact of a collision, raising the chance of severe injury or death.

question: What color are traffic control devices used in work zones?
options: a:Red.,b:Orange.,c:Yellow.
note: Orange signs, cones, and barriers warn you that you are entering 8,Special Situations & Road Users,a construction or work zone; use extra caution.

question: The best action if you become tired while driving is to:
options: a:Open a window.,b:Drink coffee.,c:Stop to rest or change drivers.
note: If you feel tired, pull over at a safe location to rest or switch drivers; brief measures are not substitutes for sleep.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What should you not assume when preparing to pass another vehicle?
options: a:Not assume the other driver will make space for you to return to your lane.,b:Assume the other driver will let you pass if you use your turn signal.,c:Assume the other driver will maintain a constant speed.
note: Never assume other drivers will make room or maintain speed; ensure there is sufficient space before passing.

question: As your blood alcohol concentration increases, you become:
options: a:More intoxicated.,b:More coordinated.,c:More sober.
note: Higher BAC levels impair judgment, coordination, and reaction time; impairment increases with BAC.

question: When weather or light conditions require lights, you should use:
options: a:Use your low beams.,b:Use your parking lights.,c:Use your high beams.
note: In fog, rain, or snow use low beam headlights; high beams can create glare and reduce visibility.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When passing on a two-lane road, what should you do first?
options: a:Sound your horn as you pass.,b:Flash your headlights as you pass.,c:Judge the distance to any oncoming vehicles.
note: Ensure there is enough distance from oncoming vehicles before starting a pass; if unsure, wait until it is safe.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If you arrive at an uncontrolled intersection at the same time as vehicles on your right and left, you should:
options: a:Wait until there are no vehicles at the intersection before proceeding.,b:Yield the right-of-way to the vehicle on your left.,c:Yield the right-of-way to the vehicle on your right.
note: When vehicles arrive simultaneously, yield to the vehicle on your right and proceed in arrival order.

question: How should you steer if the rear of your vehicle skids left?
options: a:Not turn your steering wheel.,b:Turn your steering wheel to the left to correct the skid.,c:Turn your steering wheel to the right to correct the skid.
note: On a skid, take your foot off the accelerator, avoid braking, and steer in the direction of the skid to regain control.

question: If you have consumed three beers within an hour, approximately how long will it take for the alcohol to leave your bloodstream?
options: a:Three hours.,b:One hour.,c:Two hours.
note: As a general guideline, it takes about three hours to eliminate the intoxicating effects of three standard drinks from the bloodstream, though individual factors vary.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: How should you proceed when a blocked view prevents seeing cross traffic at an intersection?
options: a:Slow down and look both ways.,b:Maintain your speed and look both ways.,c:Stop, then inch forward until you can see clearly in both directions.
note: If your vision is obstructed, stop and inch forward carefully until you can see clearly in both directions before proceeding.

question: When driving in work zones you should:
options: a:Follow the driver in front of you closely.,b:Pass the driver in front of you as soon as you can.,c:Avoid tailgating and keep a safe following distance.
note: Keep a safe distance from other vehicles, obey reduced speed limits, and watch for workers and equipment in work zones.

question: If you miss your freeway exit, what must you avoid doing?
options: a:Continue on the freeway and find an alternate route.,b:Proceed to the next exit, leave the freeway, and return to your proper exit.,c:Back up on the road or shoulder.
note: Do not back up on the freeway or shoulder; continue to the next exit and re-route from there.

question: A broken yellow line next to a solid yellow line indicates:
options: a:Passing is permitted from the side next to the broken yellow line.,b:Passing is permitted from the side next to the solid yellow line.,c:Passing is not permitted from either direction.
note: When the centerline is a solid yellow next to a broken yellow, only traffic on the broken-line side may pass; the solid side may not.

question: For quick and controlled turns, where should your hands be on the wheel?
options: a:On opposite sides of the steering wheel.,b:Next to each other on the top of the steering wheel.,c:On the top and bottom of the steering wheel.
note: Place both hands on opposite sides of the wheel (e.g., 9 and 3) for safe, controlled steering.

question: Emergency crossovers on Tennessee interstates may be used by:
options: a:To turn around when no other vehicles are present.,b:To make a U-turn when you missed your exit.,c:Emergency vehicles and highway maintenance crews only.
note: Emergency crossovers are intended for emergency vehicles and maintenance crews; they are not for general driver use or U-turns.

question: A broken yellow centerline between two lanes of traffic means:
options: a:Both lanes of traffic are going in the same direction.,b:Passing is permitted when it's safe.,c:Passing is not permitted.
note: Dashed yellow lines separate opposite-direction traffic and indicate that passing is allowed when safe and clear of oncoming vehicles.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When changing lanes you should never:
options: a:Look over your shoulder to check your blind spot.,b:Change lanes abruptly or spontaneously.,c:Check for other vehicles moving into the same lane.
note: Do not make sudden or spontaneous lane changes; check mirrors and blind spots, signal, and change lanes smoothly.

question: How far should your body be from the steering wheel for good posture?
options: a:Six to eight inches.,b:10 to 12 inches.,c:18 to 24 inches.
note: Position your body about 10 to 12 inches from the steering wheel to reduce injury risk from the airbag and ensure proper control.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: How should you perform a lane change?
options: a:Quickly and often.,b:When a car is in your blind spot.,c:Gradually and carefully.
note: Change lanes gradually and carefully, signaling and checking mirrors and blind spots to avoid collisions.

question: When parking on any hill you should:
options: a:One of your rear wheels should touch the curb.,b:Use your parking brake and leave the vehicle in "park.",c:Your front wheels should be parallel to the road, if there is no curb.
