note: Always set the parking brake and leave the transmission in gear or in Park; turn wheels appropriately depending on curb presence.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: A steady red arrow on a traffic signal means:
options: a:Drivers may turn in the indicated direction after coming to a complete stop.,b:Drivers cannot turn in the indicated direction.,c:Drivers may turn in the indicated direction.
note: A steady red arrow means traffic in that lane may not turn in the arrow's direction until a green signal is shown.

question: What is the safest action if you must pass a pedestrian while an oncoming vehicle approaches?
options: a:Slow down and let the oncoming vehicle pass first.,b:Keep driving at the same speed because the oncoming vehicle must stop.,c:Honk to get the pedestrian to move over.
note: Handle one hazard at a time: allow the oncoming vehicle to pass, then pass the pedestrian if it is safe.

question: If you see pedestrians in a crosswalk ahead, what should you do?
options: a:Pull to the right and go around the pedestrians.,b:Wait for the pedestrians to cross the street.,c:Continue ahead; the motorist has the right-of-way.
note: Drivers must yield the right-of-way to pedestrians in crosswalks and wait until they have cleared the path before proceeding.

question: A vehicle is following you too closely on a two-lane road. How should you react?
options: a:Speed up to increase the distance between you and the other car.,b:Apply your brakes to slow down, then resume your original speed.,c:Reduce your speed slowly to encourage the tailgater to drive around you.
note: If another driver is tailgating you and you cannot change lanes, slow down gradually when it is safe so the tailgater can pass. If possible, move into another lane to let them by.

question: When must you show proof of insurance to law enforcement?
options: a:Only if you are involved in a collision.,b:If you are involved in a collision or stopped for a citation.,c:Only if you are stopped and cited.
note: You must have evidence of financial responsibility and present proof of insurance when involved in a collision or when requested following a traffic stop or citation.

question: Collisions are more likely to occur when:
options: a:All vehicles are traveling at about the same speed.,b:One lane of traffic is traveling faster than the other lanes.,c:One vehicle is traveling faster or slower than the flow of traffic.
note: Crashes are more likely when a vehicle's speed differs significantly from other traffic; match the flow when it is safe and legal to do so.

question: When driving through a construction zone you should:
options: a:Decrease your following distance.,b:Pass carefully and avoid 'rubbernecking.',c:Stop to watch the workers.
note: Do not slow down to stare; drive attentively, obey signage, and maintain a safe following distance through work zones.

question: What effect does excessive speed have on crash outcomes?
options: a:Saves time.,b:Helps you maneuver around obstacles.,c:Increases the likelihood of serious bodily injury and death.
note: Excessive speed is a major contributing factor to crashes and increases the risk of serious injury and death.

question: When driving in fog you should:
options: a:Turn your lights on and off to warn other drivers.,b:Slow down and use your low beam headlights.,c:Slow down and use your high beam headlights.
note: Use low beams in fog because high beams reflect back and reduce visibility; if visibility is extremely poor, pull off safely.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Before you change lanes you should check your mirrors and also:
options: a:Always slow down in your traffic lane.,b:Glance over your shoulder.,c:Never look over your right shoulder.
note: Always check mirrors and glance over your shoulder to verify that the blind spot is clear before changing lanes.

question: When another vehicle is passing you, you should:
options: a:Brake hard.,b:Maintain a constant speed.,c:Speed up.
note: Yield to the passing vehicle by keeping a steady speed; do not speed up or brake suddenly while being passed.

question: If you see a deep puddle ahead, what is the safest action?
options: a:Avoid the puddle if possible.,b:Maintain the posted speed to make it through the water.,c:Shift into neutral as you drive through the water.
note: Avoid driving through deep puddles to reduce the risk of hydroplaning, loss of control, or hidden hazards under the water.

question: When following a motorcycle you should:
options: a:Drive more slowly.,b:Allow a larger following distance.,c:Be ready to use your horn.
note: Give motorcyclists three to four seconds of following distance because they can stop quickly and are more vulnerable.

question: Alcohol in any concentration is classified as:
options: a:A stimulant.,b:A depressant.,c:Neither of the above.
note: Alcohol is a depressant that slows nerve impulses and decreases alertness, concentration, and coordination.

question: At a school crossing sign you should:
options: a:Always sound your horn when you see children.,b:Always stop, whether there is a stop sign or not.,c:Watch for children and be ready to stop.
note: A school crossing sign warns you to be alert for children and prepared to slow or stop; only stop if signage or conditions require it.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: To avoid traffic merging from on-ramps to your right while on an interstate, what is usually best?
options: a:Change lanes to the left.,b:Slow down.,c:Maintain your speed and position.
note: When safe, move out of the right-hand lane to allow merging traffic easier access from on-ramps.

question: How should you respond if an oncoming driver does not dim bright lights?
options: a:Look toward the center of the roadway.,b:Look toward the right side of the road.,c:Look straight ahead at the headlights.
note: Look to the right edge of the road to avoid being blinded; do not retaliate by using your bright lights.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: At a yield sign you must:
options: a:Must yield to vehicles only on your right.,b:Should slow down but never stop.,c:Must yield the right-of-way to cross traffic that is close enough to cause conflict.
note: At a yield sign you must give right-of-way to traffic close enough to be a hazard before merging or crossing.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When merging into traffic after parking at a curb, you should:
options: a:Should wait for a large enough gap to get up to the speed of traffic.,b:Should drive more slowly than other traffic for 200 feet.,c:Should wait for the first two vehicles to pass, then drive into the lane.
note: Merge only when there is a gap large enough for your vehicle to reach the speed of the traffic flow safely.

question: Recent studies show the number of alcohol-related fatal crashes in Tennessee has:
options: a:Has increased.,b:Has decreased.,c:Has remained steady.
note: Data in recent years showed a reduction in the percentage of traffic fatalities that were alcohol-related.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When is it safe to pass another vehicle?
options: a:Within an intersection where there are no oncoming vehicles.,b:Wherever signs and/or pavement markings permit passing.,c:Within a curve where there are no oncoming vehicles.
note: Do not pass in intersections or where your view is blocked by curves or hills. Only pass where signs or pavement markings permit and it is safe to do so.

question: Continuous hard braking on snow or ice often:
options: a:Helps you stop faster.,b:Keeps the brakes from freezing.,c:Locks the front wheels of a vehicle, causing a loss of steering.
note: Repeated hard braking on slippery surfaces can lock wheels and cause loss of steering; use gentle braking and lower speeds.

question: When driving in fog, which headlights should you use?
options: a:Low beam headlights.,b:Four-way flashers.,c:High beam headlights.
note: Use low beams in fog, rain, or snow; high beams reflect off precipitation and reduce visibility.

question: How must you treat a flashing red traffic signal?
options: a:Come to a complete stop, yield, then proceed when clear.,b:Reduce your speed and proceed with caution.,c:Come to a complete stop and remain stopped while it flashes.
note: A flashing red signal is treated like a stop sign: stop, yield to others, and proceed when safe.

question: What is a likely consequence of tailgating other drivers?
options: a:Can frustrate other drivers and make them angry.,b:Cannot result in a traffic citation.,c:Reduces collisions by preventing being cut off.
note: Tailgating is aggressive and unsafe; it can provoke other drivers and may lead to citations or collisions.

question: Which of the following is true about driving speed?
options: a:Driving too slowly is not an unsafe practice.,b:Driving too slowly on certain highways can be dangerous.,c:The speed at which you drive a vehicle does not affect safety.
note: Driving unusually slowly can create hazards by prompting risky passing maneuvers; drive at a safe speed consistent with traffic and conditions.

question: Driving while impaired by medication is permitted:
options: a:If it is prescribed by a physician.,b:If you don't feel drowsy.,c:Under no circumstances.
note: It is illegal to drive under the influence of any substance—prescription, over-the-counter, or illegal—that impairs your driving ability.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If your wheels drop off the roadway's edge, you should:
options: a:Wait until it is safe to do so, then gradually re-enter the roadway.,b:Turn back onto the roadway immediately.,c:Stop.
note: Slow down safely, check traffic, and gradually steer back onto the pavement when it's safe rather than jerking the wheel.

question: By law, brakes on every vehicle (other than a motorcycle) must:
options: a:Not lock under any condition.,b:Consist of a good foot brake and an emergency or parking brake.,c:Consist of a good parking brake that is capable of stopping the vehicle within legal limits.
note: Tennessee law requires vehicles to have both a functioning foot brake and an emergency/parking brake.

question: A broken yellow line down the center of the road indicates:
options: a:Passing is permitted from either direction.,b:A construction zone is ahead.,c:Passing is not permitted.
note: Dashed yellow lines between opposite direction lanes mean passing is allowed when safe and when no oncoming traffic is present.

question: When you approach a pedestrian using a white cane or a guide dog, you should:
options: a:Honk your horn as you proceed past them.,b:Carefully drive around them.,c:Stop until the person is well away from your path.
note: Blind pedestrians using a cane or guide dog must be given the right-of-way; stop and wait until they are clear of your path.

question: What are potential legal consequences if you cause a fatal crash while impaired?
options: a:Be charged with vehicular homicide.,b:Be fined and sentenced to prison.,c:Both of the above.
note: Causing a fatal crash while impaired can result in vehicular homicide charges, fines, and potential imprisonment.

question: If a vehicle cuts in front of you, what is the first action to take?
options: a:Honk and step on the brake firmly.,b:Take your foot off the gas pedal.,c:Swerve into the lane next to you.
note: Remove your foot from the accelerator to increase space without making sudden moves; then brake or steer as necessary.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: It is unlawful to:
options: a:Pass another vehicle over a railroad crossing.,b:Pass another vehicle in any marked no passing zone.,c:Both of the above.
note: Passing is prohibited at locations where visibility or safety is compromised, including marked no-passing zones and at railroad crossings.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When parallel parking facing downhill, what should you do with your front wheels?
options: a:Keep your wheels straight.,b:Turn your wheels away from the side of the road.,c:Turn your wheels sharply toward the side of the road.
note: When parking downhill, turn your wheels toward the curb or edge of the road so the vehicle will roll into the curb if the brakes fail.

question: How many points on your driving record in 12 months will trigger an advisory letter for adults?
options: a:Between six and 11,b:Between eight and 10,c:12 or more
note: Adult drivers who accumulate between six and eleven points within a 12-month period will receive an advisory letter.

question: When may you cross double yellow centerlines to pass another vehicle?
options: a:When the yellow line next to your side of the road is broken.,b:If the vehicle in front moves to the right to let you pass.,c:When the yellow line next to the opposite side of the road is broken.
note: A broken yellow line next to your lane indicates passing is permitted on your side when it is safe to do so.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When is a left turn from a one-way street onto another one-way street permitted?
options: a:You increase your speed before the turn.,b:Traffic on the street moves to the right.,c:Traffic on the street moves to the left.
note: You may turn left onto a one-way street only if traffic on that street moves to the left and no sign prohibits the turn.

question: A large truck turning right onto a street with two lanes in each direction:
options: a:May complete its turn in either of the two lanes.,b:May have to swing wide to complete the right turn.,c:Must stay in the right lane at all times while turning.
note: Large trucks often need extra space and may swing wide to complete right turns due to their trailer path.

question: When following another vehicle at night, you should:
options: a:Keep your headlights on the low beam setting.,b:Use your high beam headlights.,c:Use your high beams until you are within 10 feet of the vehicle ahead.
note: Use low beams when following closely at night to avoid blinding the driver ahead; high beams should not be used near other vehicles.

question: When should you yield to a pedestrian?
options: a:Only if they are in a crosswalk.,b:At all times, even if the pedestrian is not obeying traffic laws.,c:Only if the traffic lights favor the pedestrian.
note: Do everything you can to avoid striking a pedestrian; yield as needed regardless of whether the pedestrian is obeying laws.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Who must yield when you are turning left at an intersection?
options: a:You should always yield to oncoming traffic and pedestrians.,b:Oncoming traffic and pedestrians should yield to you.,c:You should never yield to oncoming traffic and pedestrians.
note: Drivers making left turns must yield to oncoming vehicles going straight and to pedestrians in the crosswalk.

question: Large trucks are likely to lose speed when:
options: a:Driving down long, gradual hills.,b:Driving in long, gradual curves.,c:Driving up long or steep hills.
note: Trucks require more power to climb long or steep grades and often slow significantly on uphill stretches.

question: What is the definition of a crosswalk?
options: a:The area where pedestrians may cross the roadway.,b:Another name for a four-way intersection.,c:An area designated for road construction workers.
note: A crosswalk is the portion of the roadway intended for pedestrians to cross. It may be marked with solid white lines or be unmarked at some intersections.

question: Blue road signs generally provide information about:
options: a:Mileage information, such as distances to specific locations.,b:Construction and maintenance.,c:Motorist services.
note: Blue signs are service signs; they show information such as rest areas, hospitals, food, or fuel services.

question: Roads are most slippery:
options: a:Just after it starts to rain.,b:When it has been raining hard for several hours.,c:When they are clean and dry.
note: Road surfaces are especially slippery just after rain begins because oil and other residues mix with the first water.

question: Which type of road area is most likely to freeze and be slippery after precipitation?
options: a:A hilly, open road,b:A residential road,c:A road in a shaded area
note: Shaded spots freeze before other areas and remain icy longer, making them especially slippery in cold weather.

question: After you change your residence address, how long do you have to notify the Tennessee Department of Safety?
options: a:45 days.,b:10 days.,c:Six months.
note: Tennessee law requires you to report any residential address change to the Department of Safety within 10 days of the change.

question: When a school bus on your side of the road is stopped with red lights flashing, you must:
options: a:Change lanes and pass cautiously.,b:Slow to a speed no faster than 10 mph.,c:Stop until the lights stop flashing.
note: Do not proceed until the bus's red lights stop flashing and the stop arm is retracted; never pass a loading/unloading school bus.

question: When driving at night, what should you do to increase safety?
options: a:Always use your high beams.,b:Look directly at the headlights of an oncoming vehicle.,c:Increase your following distance.
note: Increase following distance at night when visibility is reduced, and use headlight beams appropriately to avoid blinding others.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: How do you know you have enough space to return to the driving lane after passing?
options: a:If the other driver signals for you to re-enter the lane.,b:If you look over your shoulder and see the passed car behind you.,c:If you can see both of the passed vehicle's headlights in your rearview mirror.
note: Only re-enter your lane when you can see the passed vehicle's headlights in your rearview mirror, ensuring a safe gap.

question: On a freeway you should look farther ahead than on a city street in order to:
options: a:Because it helps you keep up with traffic.,b:Because it takes a quarter of a mile to stop your vehicle completely.,c:See potential hazards early.
note: Looking well ahead on high-speed roads allows you to detect hazards and changing traffic conditions sooner.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: A vehicle ahead stops at a crosswalk. What must you do?
options: a:Stop and wait until all pedestrians have crossed.,b:Cautiously pass the vehicle at 10 mph or slower.,c:Change lanes and pass the stopped vehicle.
note: Do not pass a vehicle stopped at a crosswalk — there may be pedestrians you cannot see. Stop and proceed only after all pedestrians have cleared the crosswalk.

question: If you see animals standing near the roadway you should:
options: a:Quickly swerve into the next lane.,b:Slow down and proceed with caution.,c:Speed up to scare them away.
note: Slow down and be prepared to stop; animals can bolt into the road unexpectedly and may travel in groups.

question: What can happen if you mix prescription drugs and alcohol and drive?
options: a:There will likely be no effect.,b:It will make you more alert.,c:It can make you unfit to drive.
note: Combining alcohol with prescription or over-the-counter drugs can greatly impair driving ability and reaction time.

question: Which of these vehicle types is NOT required to stop before crossing any railroad grade crossing in Tennessee?
options: a:Taxis.,b:School or church buses.,c:Farm trucks hauling produce.
note: In Tennessee certain passenger and hazardous-material vehicles must always stop (e.g., school buses, taxis). Farm trucks hauling produce are not in that required-stop list.

question: Which behavior blocks the smooth flow of traffic?
options: a:Slowing down to look at a collision scene.,b:Avoiding unnecessary lane changes.,c:Using public transportation instead of your vehicle.
note: Rubbernecking — slowing to look at collisions or unusual events — causes congestion and should be avoided.

question: Using a cell phone while driving is distracting because it:
options: a:Occupies the driver's hands, eyes, and mind.,b:Causes the driver to be concerned about the cost of the call.,c:Is an activity that draws the attention of other drivers.
note: Cell phone use diverts attention from driving tasks—manual, visual, and cognitive distractions all increase crash risk.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When changing lanes you should:
options: a:Rely on the left side mirror.,b:Rely on the rearview mirror.,c:Look over your shoulder in the direction you plan to move.
note: In addition to checking mirrors and signaling, look over your shoulder to check the blind spot before changing lanes.

question: When backing up your vehicle, you should:
options: a:Press hard on the gas pedal.,b:Rely only on your rearview mirror.,c:Look directly through the rear window while backing up.
note: When reversing, look over your shoulder through the rear window and move slowly; mirrors alone do not show everything behind you.

question: If a child is riding a bicycle near your vehicle you should:
options: a:Beep your horn.,b:Expect the unexpected.,c:Expect the child to be in total control of the bicycle.
note: Children on bicycles can be unpredictable; drive cautiously and be prepared for sudden movements.

question: What should you activate if dust or smoke reduces visibility?
options: a:Emergency flashers.,b:Parking lights.,c:Headlights.
note: Turn on headlights whenever visibility is reduced so other drivers can see you; slow down until conditions improve.

question: If you are next to a single broken white line on a highway, what does that mean?
options: a:You cannot cross the line to pass.,b:You may cross the line to pass and change lanes.,c:You may only cross the line to change lanes if you are in the left lane.
note: Broken white lines separate lanes moving in the same direction; you may cross them to pass or change lanes when safe.

question: If it seems your tires have lost contact with the road surface, what should you do first?
options: a:Slow down by shifting into a lower gear.,b:Ease your foot off the gas pedal.,c:Slow down by pumping the brakes quickly and firmly.
note: If you feel a loss of traction, ease off the accelerator and avoid braking or turning until traction returns.

question: If a vehicle is equipped with airbags:
options: a:Seat belts should be worn behind the back.,b:Seat belts should still be worn.,c:Seat belts do not need to be worn.
note: Airbags are supplemental; lap and shoulder belts must still be used for maximum protection.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When entering a freeway, how should you check traffic on the freeway?
options: a:Using your rearview and side mirrors.,b:Using your rearview mirror.,c:Using your side mirror and looking over your shoulder.
note: Use mirrors and look over your shoulder to check blind spots and traffic gaps before merging onto a freeway.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When is it legal to make a left turn on a red light?
options: a:If you are traveling on a two-way street and turning onto a two-way street.,b:If you are on a one-way street turning onto another one-way street.,c:If you yield to all other traffic at the intersection.
note: After a complete stop, a left on red is allowed only when turning from a one-way street onto another one-way street and no signs prohibit it.

question: If you are near a large commercial vehicle, you should:
options: a:Drive on its right side when on curves and hills.,b:Avoid driving beside it for long stretches of time.,c:Follow the large vehicle closely to reduce wind drag on your vehicle.
note: Large commercial vehicles have big blind spots; avoid lingering beside them and ensure they can see you.

question: Which lights should you use when driving in fog?
options: a:High beam headlights.,b:Low beam headlights.,c:Four-way flashers.
note: Use low beam headlights in fog, rain, or snow because high beams will reflect back and reduce visibility.

question: To check for objects in your blind spot when changing lanes, you should:
options: a:Over your left or right shoulder.,b:Only the left outside mirror.,c:Only the inside rearview mirror.
note: Look over the appropriate shoulder to verify there is no vehicle in your blind spot before changing lanes.

question: Which statement about blind spots is correct?
options: a:Blind spots can be checked by looking in your rearview mirror.,b:Large trucks have bigger blind spots than most passenger vehicles.,c:Blind spots are eliminated if you have one outside mirror.
note: Even with mirrors, vehicles have blind spots; large trucks' blind spots are substantially larger than those of passenger cars.

question: If you park facing uphill on a street with a curb, after setting the parking brake you should:
options: a:Turn the front wheels toward the curb.,b:Turn the front wheels away from the curb.,c:Leave the front wheels straight.
note: When parking uphill with a curb, turn the wheels away from the curb so the vehicle will roll away from traffic if it moves.

question: You are in an intersection and an emergency vehicle with siren and lights is approaching. What should you do?
options: a:Pull to the right of the intersection and stop.,b:Continue through the intersection, pull to the right, and stop.,c:Stop immediately in the intersection until it passes.
note: If you are in an intersection when an emergency vehicle approaches with lights and/or siren, clear the intersection, then pull to the right and stop to yield the right-of-way.

question: When exiting the freeway on a downhill curved ramp, you should:
options: a:Wait until you have entered the curve to begin braking.,b:Slow to a safe speed before the curve.,c:Slow to the posted speed limit for the freeway.
note: Reduce your speed before entering a curve; braking while turning can cause loss of control or a skid.

question: When an oncoming car fails to dim its high beams and impairs your vision at night, what should you do?
options: a:Look straight ahead in your lane.,b:Look toward the right edge of your lane.,c:Look toward the left edge of your lane.
note: Don't look directly at the bright headlights; instead, glance toward the right edge of your lane and watch the oncoming vehicle from the corner of your eye.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: After passing a vehicle moving in the same direction, when is it safe to return to the right lane?
options: a:After about three seconds.,b:When you can no longer see the passed vehicle over your right shoulder.,c:When you can see the entire front of the passed vehicle in your rearview mirror.
note: Return to your lane only when you can clearly see the front of the passed vehicle in your rearview mirror, ensuring a safe gap.

question: The first driving-related ability that alcohol impairs is:
options: a:Balance.,b:Judgment.,c:Vision.
note: Alcohol first affects judgment and decision-making, impairing the ability to assess risks and react appropriately.

question: How can you reduce the chance of hydroplaning on a wet road?
options: a:You may hydroplane at 45 mph.,b:Hydroplaning can begin at about 35 mph.,c:Hydroplaning occurs only above 40 mph.
note: Hydroplaning can start at speeds around 35 mph on standing water because tires may not channel water away effectively at higher speeds.

question: As daylight fades, which lights should you turn on to help others see your vehicle?
options: a:Emergency flashers.,b:Low beam headlights.,c:Parking lights.
note: When daylight begins to fade, turn on your low beam headlights so other drivers can see you. Reserve high beams for open roads without oncoming traffic.

question: When following a motorcycle, you should:
options: a:Motorcycle.,b:Passenger vehicle.,c:Station wagon.
note: Allow extra space when following a motorcycle because they can stop more quickly and are harder to see, especially at night.

question: What is the likely result of continually passing other cars on a two-lane road?
options: a:Get you to your destination much more quickly and safely.,b:Increase your chances of a collision.,c:Help prevent traffic congestion.
note: Constant passing on two-lane roads increases the probability of a crash and is unsafe.

question: When parking next to a curb you should signal:
options: a:Only when pulling away from the curb.,b:When pulling next to or away from the curb.,c:When pulling next to, but not away from, the curb.
note: Signal both when pulling toward the curb and when pulling away so other drivers and pedestrians know your intention.

question: If a child appears about to run into the street, you should:
options: a:Start to prepare to slow down.,b:Flash your headlights.,c:Sound a sharp blast of your horn.
note: If a pedestrian, especially a child, is about to enter the street in front of you, sound a sharp horn to warn them if needed.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When is it appropriate to drive at the posted maximum speed limit?
options: a:During the night.,b:During the day.,c:Under ideal conditions.
note: The posted speed is only safe under ideal road and weather conditions; reduce speed when conditions are less than ideal.

question: When must a slow-moving vehicle pull over to let others pass?
options: a:At least four,b:Five or more,c:Eight or more
note: Slow-moving vehicles must pull off the roadway or otherwise allow traffic to pass when five or more vehicles are queued behind them.

question: An orange and red triangular sign displayed on a vehicle indicates:
options: a:The vehicle has the right-of-way.,b:Shoulder work ahead.,c:Slow-moving vehicle.
note: An orange-red triangle on the rear of a vehicle identifies it as a slow-moving vehicle (usually traveling 25 mph or less).

question: If you are not the first person at a crash scene and your help is not needed, you should:
options: a:Stop and look for your own curiosity.,b:Slow down to calm your nerves.,c:Drive on and not interfere with emergency procedures.
note: If emergency personnel are already handling the incident and you are not trained to assist, continue on to avoid interfering or causing additional hazards.

question: What must you do when facing a green arrow signal?
options: a:Yield to any vehicle, bicycle, or pedestrian in the intersection.,b:Wait four seconds before proceeding.,c:Yield only to pedestrians in the intersection.
note: A green arrow gives you the right to go in the arrow direction, but you must first yield to any vehicles, bicycles, or pedestrians still in the intersection.

question: Parking is illegal in which of the following locations?
options: a:Within 50 feet of a railroad crossing.,b:Both within 15 feet of a fire hydrant and within 50 feet of a railroad crossing.,c:Within 15 feet of a fire hydrant.
note: You may not park within 15 feet of a fire hydrant or within 50 feet of a railroad crossing; both are prohibited.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When may you legally block an intersection?
options: a:If you entered on a green light.,b:During rush hour.,c:Under no circumstances.
note: Never enter an intersection unless you can completely clear it; blocking an intersection is prohibited even if the light is green.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When passing another vehicle you should return to your original lane when:
options: a:You are 50 feet in front of the passed vehicle.,b:You have cleared the front bumper of the passed vehicle.,c:You can see both headlights of the passed vehicle in your rearview mirror.
note: Return to your lane only after you can see the passed vehicle's headlights in your rearview mirror, indicating adequate space.

question: On the freeway behind a large truck, you should follow:
options: a:No more than one car length behind the truck so the driver can see you.,b:Farther behind the truck than you would when following a passenger vehicle.,c:Closely behind the truck in bad weather because the driver can see farther ahead than you can.
note: Leave extra following distance behind large trucks because they block your view and require longer stopping distances.

question: How can you reduce the risk of hydroplaning in rain?
options: a:Drive at a speed suitable for ideal conditions.,b:Apply your brakes as soon as the car starts to skid.,c:Slow down.
note: Reduce speed in wet conditions to allow tires to maintain contact with the road and avoid hydroplaning.

question: On roadways, bicycles are considered:
options: a:Hazards.,b:Vehicles.,c:Dangerous.
note: Bicycles are legally treated as vehicles; cyclists must follow the same rules of the road as motor vehicles.

question: During rainy weather, when should you be most cautious when turning or stopping?
options: a:One half hour after it stops raining.,b:During the first half hour of rain.,c:After it has been raining all day.
note: Be extra careful during the first half hour of rain when oil on the road can mix with water and create slippery conditions for turning and stopping.

question: Alcohol is classified as which type of drug?
options: a:A stimulant.,b:An antihistamine.,c:A depressant.
note: Alcohol is a depressant that slows the central nervous system, impairs judgment, and reduces reflexes.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Where is a U-turn not permitted?
options: a:In a parking lot.,b:On or near any curve or hill.,c:On a straight roadway with a clear view for 500 feet in both directions.
note: Never make a U-turn on or near a curve or hill where you cannot see oncoming traffic or pedestrians clearly.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What should you do if you see a steady yellow light and are not yet in the intersection?
options: a:Speed up to beat the red light.,b:Reduce your speed and proceed carefully through the intersection.,c:Come to a safe stop.
note: A steady yellow warns the light will turn red; if you have not entered, you should safely stop rather than run the light.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Which of the following is NOT a safe practice on the interstate?
options: a:If you miss your exit, you must go to the next exit.,b:Slower traffic must keep to the right.,c:Change lanes without signaling.
note: Always signal lane changes. On interstates, slower vehicles should remain to the right and you should use the next exit if you miss yours.

question: Which statement about medications and driving is correct?
options: a:Most cold and allergy medicines can cause drowsiness.,b:Over-the-counter medicines never affect driving when taken as directed.,c:Medications prescribed by a doctor are always safe to take before driving.
note: Both prescription and over-the-counter medicines can impair driving; cold and allergy drugs often cause drowsiness.

question: Before switching on the ignition, what safety action should you take?
options: a:Buckle your safety belt.,b:Be sure all passengers have buckled their safety belts.,c:Both of the above.
note: Develop a routine: buckle your seat belt and ensure all passengers are buckled before starting the vehicle.

question: If a tire suddenly blows out while you are driving, what should you do?
options: a:Apply the brakes firmly.,b:Use the brakes lightly.,c:Pump the brakes.
note: If a tire goes flat, hold the steering wheel steady, take your foot off the accelerator, and slow gradually using light braking. Avoid hard braking or sudden steering movements.

question: What should you do if your vehicle starts to skid?
options: a:Pump the brakes.,b:Apply the brakes lightly.,c:Stay off 8,Special Situations & Road Users,the brakes.
note: If your vehicle begins to skid, avoid braking; steer to correct the skid until control is regained.

question: If the rear of your car starts skidding to the left, what is the correct steering action?
options: a:Steer to the right.,b:Steer to the left.,c:Tap your brakes lightly and shift into neutral.
note: When the rear skids left, steer left (in the direction you want the car to go) to regain control; avoid heavy braking.

question: Which factor listed affects how quickly a person absorbs alcohol?
options: a:Weight,b:Height,c:Intelligence
note: Factors such as body weight, biological sex, food in the stomach, and the number of drinks affect alcohol absorption; only time removes alcohol from the body.

question: Backing up a vehicle is:
options: a:Only dangerous in large vehicles.,b:Dangerous if you have a helper.,c:Always dangerous.
note: Reversing is inherently risky because visibility is limited; use care and helpers or cameras when available.

question: If you park facing uphill with no curb, you should set the parking brake and:
options: a:Keep your wheels facing straight.,b:Turn your wheels toward the edge of the road.,c:Turn your wheels away from the edge of the road.
note: When parking uphill without a curb, turn the front wheels toward the edge of the road so the vehicle will roll off the roadway rather than into traffic if it moves.

question: When driving in fog or mist you should not use high beam headlights because:
options: a:Vehicles behind you may follow too closely.,b:The light will reflect back into your eyes.,c:Approaching vehicles might not see you.
note: High beams reflect off fog and mist and reduce your visibility by creating glare; use low beams instead.

question: When should you increase your following distance to allow extra space?
options: a:When following a station wagon.,b:When following a driver who cannot see the rear of their vehicle.,c:When following a small passenger car.
note: Give extra space behind large vehicles, trailers, or vehicles with limited rear visibility because they may not see you.

question: As your speed increases, it becomes more important to:
options: a:Change lanes frequently.,b:Turn on your headlights.,c:Look well ahead of your vehicle.
note: Higher speeds require scanning farther ahead to detect hazards and allow more time to react.

question: To view vehicles in your blind spots you should check:
options: a:Over your shoulders.,b:The outside rearview mirror.,c:The inside rearview mirror.
note: Blind spots are areas not visible in mirrors; a quick shoulder check reveals vehicles beside you.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: A steady green traffic light at an intersection means:
options: a:Increase your speed.,b:Adjust your mirrors.,c:You may continue through the intersection at a safe and reasonable speed if it is clear.
note: A steady green signal allows you to proceed, but you must yield to traffic and pedestrians already in the intersection and go only when clear.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Drivers turning left must yield to:
options: a:Overtaking cars.,b:Oncoming cars.,c:No one.
note: A vehicle turning left must yield to oncoming traffic that is proceeding straight or making a lawful turn.

question: If your vehicle becomes disabled on the highway, you should:
options: a:Stop where you are.,b:Park with all four wheels off the traveled highway, if possible.,c:Stop in the right lane.
note: If possible, move your vehicle completely off the main-traveled portion of the road to avoid blocking traffic and to stay safe.

question: If your vehicle develops a mechanical problem while driving you should:
options: a:Signal and pull into the slow lane.,b:Put on your hazard lights and pull off the road.,c:Stop in your lane and put on your hazard lights.
note: If possible, get your vehicle off the roadway, activate your hazards, and remain in the vehicle away from traffic.

question: How should you change your driving when the road is wet or icy?
options: a:Reduce your speed.,b:Drive at the posted speed.,c:Speed up.
note: Tires have less traction on wet or icy pavement; reduce speed and drive more cautiously.

question: What is the legal status of holding a driver's license?
options: a:Right, not a privilege.,b:Privilege, not a right.,c:Requirement.
note: A driver's license is a privilege granted by the state and must be earned and maintained under the law.

question: When are you permitted to double park?
options: a:To load or unload passengers.,b:On a four-lane street only.,c:Never.
note: Double parking is prohibited; do not park alongside a legally parked vehicle on the roadway.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When making a left turn at an intersection you should:
options: a:Oncoming traffic and pedestrians should yield to you.,b:You should always yield to oncoming traffic and pedestrians.,c:You should never yield to oncoming traffic and pedestrians.
note: Yield to oncoming vehicles and pedestrians when completing a left turn; only turn when the way is clear and legal.

question: Your vehicle's wheels have slipped off the pavement edge. What is the first thing you should do?
options: a:Apply the brakes and turn the front wheels sharply to the left.,b:Turn the front wheels slightly to the left to edge the car back onto the pavement.,c:Hold the steering wheel firmly, release the gas pedal, and gently apply the brakes.
note: If your vehicle leaves the roadway, keep a firm grip on the wheel, take your foot off the gas, and gently apply the brakes until you slow. Once you have reduced speed and checked for traffic, return safely to the road. Do not jerk the wheel to immediately re-enter traffic.

question: What penalties apply on a first DUI conviction when the driver has no prior DUI convictions?
options: a:A $100 fine, 24 hours in jail, and a six-month revocation.,b:A $500 fine, 12 hours in jail, and a three-month revocation.,c:A $350 fine, 48 hours in jail, and a one-year revocation.
note: A first DUI conviction typically includes a jail sentence of at least 48 hours (longer if BAC ≥ 0.20), fines between $350–$1,500, and a one-year license revocation.

question: If your vehicle has a lap and shoulder belt system, you should:
options: a:Use both the lap and shoulder belts.,b:Use only the lap belt.,c:Use only the shoulder belt.
note: Always wear both the lap and shoulder portions of a two-part belt system for full protection.

question: What term describes the amount of alcohol in a person's blood?
options: a:Implied consent (IC).,b:Blood alcohol concentration (BAC).,c:Rate of alcohol consumption (RAC).
note: Blood Alcohol Concentration (BAC) measures the percentage of alcohol in the blood; higher BAC indicates greater impairment.

question: To avoid skidding on slippery surfaces, you should:
options: a:Speed up to enter curves and slow down to exit them.,b:Slow down before entering curves and intersections.,c:Shift to a lower gear after starting down a steep hill.
note: Reduce speed before entering curves or intersections; entering a curve too fast increases the risk of skidding.

question: In which situation should your wheels NOT be pointed straight ahead?
options: a:When parked on the side of a level roadway where there is no curb.,b:When waiting to make a left turn at a traffic light.,c:When parked on a hill or sloping driveway.
note: When parked on a slope, turn the wheels so the vehicle will roll away from traffic or into the curb if the brakes fail.

question: Before entering a curve you should:
options: a:Activate your turn signal.,b:Reduce your speed.,c:Brake hard.
note: Reduce speed before entering a curve to maintain control; braking while turning can cause loss of traction.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If a police officer directs you to go through a red light without stopping, you should:
options: a:Come to a complete stop before proceeding.,b:Go through the intersection without stopping as directed.,c:Stop until the light turns green.
note: Instructions from a police officer directing traffic override traffic signals; follow the officer's directions.

question: If it is very foggy, slow down and:
options: a:Turn your lights to their high beam setting.,b:Turn on your emergency flashers.,c:Turn your lights to their low beam setting.
note: In heavy fog, use low beam headlights (and fog lights if equipped) to reduce glare and improve visibility.

question: What is true about driving in roadwork zones?
options: a:Fines are the same as in normal areas.,b:You must Slow for the Cone Zone, c:Slow only if you think workers are present.”
note: Work zones often have increased fines and special warnings; observe signs and slow down for the Cone Zone.

question: If the centerline is one solid yellow and one broken yellow and the broken line is next to your lane, what does that mean?
options: a:You are not allowed to pass in this area.,b:You are in a passing zone and may pass if no oncoming traffic is present.,c:You are only allowed to make right turns in this area.
note: A broken yellow line next to your lane means you may pass when it is safe and no oncoming traffic is present; the solid line prohibits passing from the other side.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: After passing a vehicle, it is safe to return to your lane when:
options: a:The driver you passed signals for you to return to your lane.,b:You signal your intention for three seconds.,c:You see the headlights of the passed vehicle in your rearview mirror.
note: Return to the travel lane when you can see the passed vehicle's headlights in your rearview mirror, indicating a safe gap.

question: What does a broken yellow centerline next to your lane allow?
options: a:Passing is not permitted.,b:Passing on the right is permitted when the way ahead is clear.,c:Passing on the left is permitted when the way ahead is clear.
note: A broken yellow line beside your lane indicates you may cross to pass on the left when the way is clear and safe.

question: When should you use your vehicle's horn?
options: a:Another driver makes a mistake.,b:It may help prevent a collision.,c:Another vehicle is in your way.
note: Use the horn only when necessary to avoid collisions, not to express anger or attempt to force another driver to move.

question: How close to the curb must your wheels be when parallel parked?
options: a:Within two feet of the curb.,b:Within 18 inches of the curb.,c:Within one foot of the curb.
note: When parallel parking, you must be within 18 inches of the curb to be parked legally and safely.

question: Why should drivers give extra space to children on bicycles?
options: a:They do not have the same physical reflexes as adults.,b:They are smaller and more difficult to see than adults.,c:Both of the above.
note: Children are less predictable and harder to see; allow extra room and be especially alert near schools and play areas.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If you want to enter the freeway but don't see a gap in traffic, what should you do on the ramp?
options: a:Maintain your speed and force other drivers to create a gap.,b:Slow down on the ramp to wait for a gap.,c:Stop at the end of the ramp to wait for a gap.
note: If no gap is available, slow down on the ramp to wait; stopping at the end of the ramp can leave you unable to accelerate to freeway speed safely.

question: A flashing red traffic light indicates you must:
options: a:Treat the intersection as if it is controlled by a stop sign.,b:May not proceed until it changes to green.,c:Are traveling in the wrong direction.
note: A flashing red light means stop completely, then proceed only when the way is clear, just like a stop sign.

question: Where should your hands be placed on the steering wheel to turn quickly and safely?
options: a:9 o'clock and 3 o'clock positions.,b:11 o'clock and 6 o'clock positions.,c:7 o'clock and 5 o'clock positions.
note: Place your hands on opposite sides of the wheel (9 and 3) for better control and balance during quick maneuvers.

question: What is the only proven way to eliminate alcohol from your system?
options: a:Breathe in some fresh air.,b:Give your body time.,c:Drink coffee.
note: Only time allows the body to metabolize alcohol; coffee, cold showers, or exercise do not lower BAC.

question: Which action demonstrates defensive driving?
options: a:Put one car length between you and the car ahead.,b:Look only at the car in front of you while driving.,c:Keep your eyes moving to scan for hazards.
note: Defensive driving requires constantly scanning the road and surroundings, not staring only at the vehicle ahead.

question: When passing a motorcycle, what must you do?
options: a:Stay in the right lane as much as possible.,b:Blow your horn to make the motorcycle move onto the shoulder.,c:Have your vehicle entirely in the left lane before and during the pass.
note: Give motorcycles a full lane; do not share a lane with them and ensure you are fully in the passing lane before and during the maneuver.

question: How should you make room for vehicles merging onto the freeway?
options: a:Slowing down.,b:Merging into a different lane.,c:Maintaining your speed and position.
note: If possible, change lanes to create a gap for entering vehicles; if you cannot, adjust your speed to allow a safe merge.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: A major contributing factor in fatal traffic crashes in Tennessee is:
options: a:Following too closely.,b:Speeding.,c:Turning into the wrong lane.
note: Traveling at speeds above safe or posted limits is a major factor in severe and fatal crashes.

question: What is the correct immediate action if a tire blows out?
options: a:Apply the brake and hold it.,b:Hold the steering wheel tightly and use the brakes lightly.,c:Pull over quickly without slowing down gradually.
note: Grip the steering wheel firmly, ease off the gas, and brake lightly as you slow and steer to a safe place off the road.

question: What does a broken yellow centerline indicate?
options: a:Passing is not permitted.,b:Passing on the right is permitted when the way ahead is clear.,c:Passing on the left is permitted when the way ahead is clear.
note: A broken yellow line beside your lane indicates that you may cross the centerline to pass when it is safe and clear of oncoming traffic.

question: Which lights should you use to improve visibility in rain or fog?
options: a:Parking lights,b:Low beam headlights,c:High beam headlights
note: Use low-beam headlights in rain, snow, sleet, or fog; high beams can reflect off precipitation and reduce visibility.

question: If a pedestrian with a guide dog is waiting to cross where you want to turn right, you should:
options: a:Tell the pedestrian when to cross the street.,b:Turn off your engine until the person crosses the street.,c:Wait until the person crosses the street.
note: Pedestrians using a cane or guide dog must be given the right-of-way; wait until they have crossed safely before turning.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Under which road marking condition are you permitted to pass?
options: a:You are on a hill or curve.,b:You are on a road with a solid line next to your lane.,c:You are on a road with a broken line next to your lane.
note: A broken centerline on your side means you may pass another vehicle on the left when it is safe to do so.

question: After several alcoholic drinks, the only thing that reduces the impairment is:
options: a:Drinking several cups of coffee.,b:Taking a cold shower.,c:Waiting several hours.
note: Only time allows the body to metabolize alcohol and reduce its impairing effects; remedies like coffee or showers do not speed this process.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When is it illegal to make a U-turn near a curve or hill?
options: a:Drive on the shoulder of the road.,b:See at least 500 feet in each direction.,c:Make the turn within 30 seconds.
note: Do not make a U-turn where you cannot clearly see traffic for at least 500 feet in both directions.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: After passing a vehicle on the left, it is safe to return to the right lane when:
options: a:When you can no longer see the vehicle over your right shoulder.,b:When you can see the front of the passed vehicle in your rearview mirror.,c:After about three seconds.
note: Return to your lane only after you can clearly see the front of the vehicle you passed in your rearview mirror.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When you want to change lanes you should never:
options: a:Check your blind spot by looking over your shoulder.,b:Check for other drivers moving into the same lane.,c:Move into another lane while within an intersection.
note: Do not change lanes within an intersection; always check mirrors and blind spots before moving across lanes.

question: Which action helps reduce the chance of road rage incidents?
options: a:Always signal your intention when changing lanes.,b:Talk on your cell phone while driving.,c:Use your horn frequently.
note: Signal intentions and obey traffic laws to avoid misunderstandings and reduce the chance of confrontation with other drivers.

question: If a truck or bus is making a right turn where you also intend to turn right, you should:
options: a:Quickly turn before the truck or bus is able to.,b:Wait until the truck or bus completes its turn before you turn.,c:Squeeze between the truck or bus and the curb.
note: Do not try to cut between a turning large vehicle and the curb; wait until it has finished turning to avoid a collision.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Which lane should you use to make a left turn from a one-way street?
options: a:The lane nearest the left curb.,b:The lane nearest the center of the street.,c:The lane nearest the right curb.
note: When turning, start from the lane closest to the direction you wish to go; on a one-way street, make a left turn from the lane nearest the left curb.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When is it appropriate to yield your right-of-way?
options: a:Often, even at controlled intersections.,b:Whenever it helps prevent collisions.,c:Never because it confuses other drivers.
note: Yield your right-of-way whenever doing so will help avoid a crash; safety is more important than insisting on right-of-way.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Should you ever start across an intersection if you know you will block it when the light turns red?
options: a:Under any circumstances.,b:Unless you entered the intersection on a yellow light.,c:Unless you entered the intersection on a green light.
note: Do not enter an intersection unless you can clear it before the signal turns red; blocking an intersection is prohibited and punishable.

question: Which precaution is important when driving at night?
options: a:Always use your high beams.,b:Look directly at the headlights of an oncoming vehicle.,c:Increase your following distance.
note: Night driving reduces visibility and judgment of distance; increase following distance and use appropriate lighting.

question: Which is a safe driving technique?
options: a:Using your high beam lights in the fog.,b:Checking your rearview mirrors frequently.,c:Staring at the road ahead of your vehicle.
note: Scan the road and check mirrors every few seconds; do not stare at one spot and do not use high beams in fog.

question: What is the only way to lower BAC and reduce alcohol's effects?
options: a:Drinking caffeinated beverages.,b:Eating high-fat foods.,c:Allowing time for the body to metabolize the alcohol.
note: Only time will sober you; nothing you eat or drink can speed up alcohol elimination.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What steps should you take before changing lanes or passing?
options: a:Check your blind spots and mirrors.,b:Signal your intention before changing lanes.,c:Both of the above.
note: Always signal and check mirrors and blind spots before changing lanes to ensure it is safe.

question: What is the correct response to a sudden tire blowout?
options: a:Grip the steering wheel firmly, slow down, and move out of the traffic lane.,b:Pump the brakes rapidly.,c:Brake hard and steer immediately to the road edge.
note: Hold the wheel firmly, ease off the gas to slow, lightly apply brakes when safe, and exit the traffic lane gradually.

question: You should avoid sudden stops in front of large trucks and buses because:
options: a:Large trucks and buses, due to their size and weight, require longer distances to stop than smaller passenger vehicles.,b:Small vehicle drivers cannot adequately see large trucks and buses in their rearview mirrors.,c:Large trucks and buses travel at a higher speeds than small vehicles.
note: Large vehicles need more distance to stop; sudden stops in front of them increase the risk of a rear-end collision.

question: On a multilane road, a solid yellow line beside a dashed yellow line means:
options: a:Passing is permitted only from the direction next to the dashed line.,b:Passing is permitted from both directions.,c:Passing is prohibited from both directions.
note: Where a solid and a dashed yellow centerline appear together, traffic adjacent to the dashed line may cross to pass; traffic adjacent to the solid line may not.

question: Slowing down just to look at collisions or unusual events typically:
options: a:Improves traffic flow by preventing collisions.,b:Prevents rear-end collisions.,c:Causes traffic congestion.
note: 'Rubbernecking' creates slowdowns and congestion and can cause additional collisions; keep moving safely.

question: Blind spots are:
options: a:Traffic control devices.,b:Spots in your vision when you become fatigued.,c:Areas that cannot be seen in a vehicle's mirrors.
note: Blind spots are areas near the rear corners of your vehicle that cannot be seen by using the mirrors alone; check over your shoulder.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: At a red light with a green arrow, when may you go in the arrow's direction?
options: a:If you are in the proper lane and the intersection is clear.,b:After first coming to a complete stop.,c:Only after waiting for the light to change.
note: A green arrow allows movement in the arrow's direction from the proper lane when the way is clear; yield to pedestrians and vehicles already in the intersection.

question: How should you brake on snow or ice if your vehicle has ABS?
options: a:Pump the brakes.,b:Press and hold the brake pedal firmly.,c:Stay off the brakes and wait for the car to drift to a stop.
note: With ABS, press and hold the brake pedal firmly; the system will automatically apply and release the brakes as needed.
